invariant_findings.invariant: 2. FEE MODEL: live uses 0.07·p·(1-p) winner-only; backtest used legacy 2%-on-profit
invariant_findings.detail: Live engine poly_updown_resolver.py imports slot_resolution_pnl from backend.app.venues.polymarket.fees (poly_updown_resolver.py:67). Per FIDELITY_AUDIT_MOMO_SHADOW_2026_05_29.md §4 and DEBUG_FINDINGS_2026_05_29.md line 19, that function uses POLYMARKET_RESOLUTION_FEE_RATE=0.07 via apply_resolution_fee(): fee = 0.07·p·(1-p), winner-only. CLAUDE.md and HANDOFF_2026_05_22 verify production actually charges legacy 2%-on-profit (pnl_won = qty·(1-entry_price)·0.98, no fee on losses). The momo_v2 creating backtests (MOMO_FULL_BACKTEST_WS_2026_05_06.md, validated by HANDOFF) used LegacyConfig. The live resolver thus overstates fees ~2.4× at p=0.65, making shadow PnL systematically understated vs what real production would show. This is a persistent known DISCREPANCY.

invariant_findings.invariant: 3. L25 FILL + SPREAD FILTER: live uses WS BookMirror + same-token bid-ask; backtest spread filter may differ
invariant_findings.detail: Live: books fetched from WS BookMirror via paper_executor.get_orderbook_snapshot at t+60 (poly_updown_loop.py:841-857). Spread stored as BarContext.spread_pct_yes/no from _spread_pct() — same-token bid-ask on each side. CLAUDE.md invariant warns live controller polymarket_sniper_v5.py uses cross-token spread abs(up_vwap-(1-dn_vwap)); however momo_v2's controller (polymarket_updown.py) uses _spread_pct() which is same-token, matching engine_v2 backtest behavior for this family. The momo_v2 backtest (MOMO_FULL_BACKTEST_WS_2026_05_06.md) used engine_v2 with same-token spread. This is consistent. L25 subsample issue: momo_v2 backtests used native 10Hz L25 per spec compliance. verdict.note: All material claims check out. (1) Fix spec TV_AGENT_FIX_MOMO_V2_BUGS_2026_05_21.md line 113 explicitly lists this sleeve for immediate disable — verified. (2) main.py:1679-1681 has a literal comment "No per-policy CSV gate (v2 spec is 'spawn all 18')"; the _DEPRECATED_POLY_UPDOWN_SLEEVE_IDS filter at lines 1700-1703 only strips sleeve IDs from the logged `sleeve_ids` tuple but does NOT prevent the controller from being appended to `_all_controllers` at line 1711-1712 unconditionally, so the controller ends up in momo_v2_controllers (poly_updown_loop.py:1661-1665) and fires at every t+60s boundary — the deprecation env var provides no actual fire suppression. (3) firing_sleeves_7d.csv confirms 60 fires in 7d (8.6/day), WR 0.417, PnL -$280.32. (4) The catastrophic DOWN-direction pattern is real per the fix spec's own 14d table (eth_5m_v2+F7: 91% of DOWN bets resolved UP); the 41.7% live WR is consistent with this. One minor imprecision: the claim describes the pattern as "DOWN+RSI<50" but the spec characterises it as F7-confirmed DOWN bets generally (RSI threshold is implicit in f7_passes, not an explicit cell filter). Severity stays high: paper-only so no real capital at risk, but the sleeve is definitively misfiring and the disable action from a May 2026 spec has not been executed as of the Jun 1 snapshot.
verdict.evidence: vps3_engine_snapshot_2026_06_01/engine/main.py:1679-1712 (no per-cell kill; deprecation filter is logging-only); vps3_engine_snapshot_2026_06_01/engine/poly_updown_loop.py:1661-1665 (momo_v2_controllers list includes all 3 policy controllers without exclusion); vps3_engine_snapshot_2026_06_01/api/bots.py:313-317 (TV_POLY_DEPRECATED_SLEEVES env var exists but only affects dashboard manifest, not fire execution); vps3_engine_snapshot_2026_06_01/firing_sleeves_7d.csv:63 (60 fires, WR=0.417, PnL=-280.32); strategy_lab/reports/TV_AGENT_FIX_MOMO_V2_BUGS_2026_05_21.md:111-124 (Action 1 disable list at line 113, includes this sleeve); strategy_lab/reports/TV_AGENT_FIX_MOMO_V2_BUGS_2026_05_21.md:93-103 (14d table: eth_5m_v2+F7 DOWN fires resolve UP 91%)

verdict.note: The claim misidentifies this as an active code-level BUG mandating an un-actioned disable. Three material errors weaken it to low-severity noise. First, the "fix spec lines 121-123" are from `TV_AGENT_FIX_MOMO_V2_BUGS_2026_05_21.md` (a yaml block listing the sleeve for disable), but that spec was superseded the same day by `EXACT_BUG_MOMO_V2_QTY_COMPUTE_ASYMMETRY_2026_05_21.md`, which explicitly retracts the "code bug" finding: "Confirmed code bugs in production momo / momo_v2 / F7 stack: 0." The retraction identifies the 17.65% / -41pp pattern as a regime artifact of `_compute_qty_shares` [0.05, 0.95] filtering asymmetrically during a 23.5h strongly-trending window, not a signal-logic defect. Second, by 2026-05-29 `BACKTEST_VS_LIVE_MOMO_2026_05_29.md` records the sleeve at n_live=11, 72.7% WR, +$11.39/tr with verdict MATCH, and the sleeve is listed as active (YES) in `SLEEVE_INVENTORY_VPS3_2026_05_31.md` at line 207. Third, `FIDELITY_LIVE_B_momo_f7_2026_06_01.md` is the definitive June-1 audit of this exact family; it concludes BUG count=0 / DRIFT=0 for all 21 checks, calling the 15m cells "net-positive" and the losses "FAITHFUL DECAY — not a bug." The main.py:1683 registration is conditional on `TV_POLY_MOMO_V2_ENABLED=true` (lines 1675-1683), not unconditional. The current 7d data (15 fires, 40% WR, -$77.03 per `firing_sleeves_7d.csv`) is a small-n variance concern on a sleeve whose backtest WR is ~54-55% (CLEAN_BACKTEST_PHASE_B_FINAL_2026_05_21 line 63), not evidence of the "catastrophic -41pp" pattern. What remains real: the sleeve has no Markov overlay (bare F7 only), the 5-day sample at 40% is on the wrong side of neutral, and the original spec's disable recommendation was never formally cleared with a written supersede notice on the original file. That warrants monitoring and possible pausing, but at low severity as a performance concern, not a code bug requiring emergency disable.

audit.engine_summary: Signal anchor: fire_us = slot_start_us + offset_s * 1_000_000 (poly_sniper_v5_loop.py:145). Gates evaluate at fire_us against TV-native panels (regime_panel, tr_panel, rf_panel, ta_indicators, vol_hurst_panel, f7_v7_panel, microprice_panel). This is NOT the momo ws_s anchor — sniper-v5 sleeves intentionally evaluate at offset time, not pre-window. Fee model: operator-confirmed as 0.07*p*(1-p) winner-only curve ('curve_winner' in maker/base.py:132-144), i.e. pnl_won = shares*(1-vwap)*(1 - 0.07*vwap), no fee on losers (maker/base.py:141-146). Fill model: L25 BookMirror walk at fire_us via paper_executor.get_orderbook_snapshot (main.py:2390), 25ms WS native (subsample_1hz=False). Spread filter: per-sleeve _SPREAD_SOL = Decimal('0.025') (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:199); applied as same-token ask0-bid0 check via fill_at_book. Exit: HOLD to slot_end + 60s RESOLUTION_BUFFER_S oracle call for all SOL 5m sleeves (loop:197-230); no HEDGE_LATE or LAG_REVERSAL_STOP for any SOL 5m sleeve. Sizing: notional_usd_override=None for all SOL 5m sleeves → default $25. V9 B1/B2/B3 polymarket flow gates use in-memory V9DataStore trade buffer (sniper_v5_v9_data.py). A2 HL cascade gate uses cex_liq_feed (CEX futures liquidations from okx/bybit/gate/bitget).

invariant_findings.invariant: 1. SIGNAL ANCHOR
invariant_findings.detail: Sniper-v5 is NOT a momo/F7 sleeve. fire_us = slot_start_us + offset_s * 1e6 (loop.py:145). Gates evaluate panel data at fire_us, not at ws_s = slot_start - window_s. This is correct per spec — the sniper architecture intentionally fires at intra-slot offsets to read panels that have warmed up by that time. No lookahead is introduced. The ws_s anchor invariant applies only to F7/momo sleeves, none of which are in this family.

invariant_findings.invariant: 2. FEE MODEL
invariant_findings.detail: Live engine uses 0.07*p*(1-p) winner-only ('curve_winner'): confirmed by operator in HANDOFF_2026_06_01 ('fee model = 0.07*p*(1-p) winner-only is CORRECT, operator-confirmed') and implemented in maker/base.py:132-146. The one available SOL 5m backtest (SOLRF_FULLPERIOD_2026_05_31.md) explicitly used 'legacy 2%-on-profit' fee (SOLRF report line 29: 'All numbers in tables below use legacy 2%-on-profit fee'). No SOL 5m sniper universe panel exists (see invariant 5). The V6/V7/V8/V9 sleeve search panels — the actual creating backtests — also used legacy_2pct per SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_V9_AND_VL spec §0: 'fee_model = legacy_2pct_profit'. The 0.07 curve charges ~2x more fees at median vwap=0.65 vs legacy 2%: at p=0.65 curve pays 0.07*0.65*0.35*shares = 1.59% per share vs legacy 2%*(1-0.65)=0.70% per share — so the live fee is actually higher than the backtest fee for high-vwap SOL entries, meaning live PnL is systematically lower than backtest PnL for winning trades.

invariant_findings.invariant: 3. L25 FILL AND SPREAD FILTER
invariant_findings.detail: Live uses WS BookMirror (confirmed: main.py:2390 book_snapshot_fn=paper_executor.get_orderbook_snapshot, WS-native 10Hz). Spread filter in live code: _SPREAD_SOL = Decimal('0.025') in sniper_v5_sleeves.py:199 applied per-sleeve. The exact spread comparison used in fill_at_book is not visible in this snapshot (controller code is backend-only, not in the snapshot), but CLAUDE.md documents that live uses cross-token spread abs(up_vwap-(1-dn_vwap)) while engine_v2 backtest uses same-token ask0-bid0. These two metrics diverge significantly on thin SOL books. No SOL 5m universe panel exists so the backtest spread filter cannot be verified. SOLRF report used approximate gate reconstruction with 'exact live thresholds unknown' (SOLRF p.18). The SOL canonical L25 is 'genuinely thin' per HANDOFF (empty asks = real market). (2) Line number citation is wrong: "SOLRF_FULLPERIOD_2026_05_31.md line 46" actually shows "base + drop_US | WR 59.9% | -$578" — the WR 57.7% / -$2,015 at offset=120s is at line 67 (offset sensitivity table, base rf+tr variant). (4) The fee direction makes the divergence worse, not better: SOLRF used legacy 2%-on-profit (SOLRF line 27-29) while live uses the 0.07 curve (AUDIT_FINAL_CORRECTED line 4,12); at vwap 0.639, the curve is approximately 2.2x more expensive per winning trade, so the live fee is MORE costly than the backtest fee. (5) The master audit (MASTER_LIVE_VS_BACKTEST_2026_05_29.md line 78) explicitly flags the SOL L25 as "bt unverifiable" (55% NaN asks in canonical data), meaning no reliable fill replay exists — the backtest numbers for this sleeve are built on approximate gate reconstruction (SOLRF line 16: "APPROXIMATE — exact live thresholds unknown") and unverifiable fills. Correct severity is medium: the positive live PnL vs negative backtest is real and warrants monitoring, but the comparison is not apple-to-apple (wrong gate set in backtest, unverifiable L25 fills, approximate thresholds, different fee model), and the claim's specific code/line citations are wrong. All core claims verify against the code and reports. sniper_v5_sleeves.py:327-342 exactly matches the claimed gate stack (g_rf_strict_align, g_tr_above_ema200, g_tr_above_pp, g_tr_partial_stack_with, offsets 90/120/150/180, spread=0.025), and FIDELITY_AUDIT_V5_V9_2026_05_29.md line 26 confirms the live implementation is a MATCH to spec. The fee-mismatch concern is real: SOLRF confirmed the approximate backtest predates the fee model clarification (legacy 2%-on-profit is production truth). One minor overstatement in the original claim: calling the gate "entirely untested" is slightly strong because the gate-approximated spread-sim did run it — but given the approximations diverge from live semantics and the result is negative, the conclusion (no valid OOS validation) stands. Severity remains high: the sleeve is net-negative in the only available backtest, sub-breakeven WR (70% vs ~64% breakeven but entry vwaps are high, pushing breakeven higher), n too small to overcome sampling noise, and the most recent portfolio analysis already marked it for removal.

verdict.evidence: Code verified at sniper_v5_sleeves.py:538-550 (gates correct), sniper_v5_thresholds.py:84 (MP_NO_EXTREME_150_BPS_THR=150.0 confirmed — claim cited wrong filename "thresholds.py"), and sniper_v5_gates.py:1439-1446 (g_mp_no_extreme_150 returns False when |mp_skew_bps| >= 150 OR s is None). The 1-fire rate is confirmed in firing_sleeves_7d.csv line 154. The definitive proof of which gate is blocking: sibling sleeve V6_06 (poly_sniper_v5_sol_5m_f7_mfi_ema200_vwap_v6) uses identical gates except mfi_with instead of g_mp_no_extreme_150 and fires 608 times (WR 68.8%) — so g_vwap_in_55_80 is NOT the bottleneck on SOL; g_mp_no_extreme_150 is the sole blocker. However the claim contains two errors that reduce severity: (1) it inverts the gate semantics — the claim says "skew values large enough to exceed 0 but small enough to stay under 150" but the gate PASSES when |skew| < 150 and BLOCKS when |skew| >= 150 bps, meaning SOL's inherently higher microprice volatility is the more plausible cause (not a feed-population issue); (2) the claim says "No OOS panel" but SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_V6_SELECTED_2026_05_27.md §05 documents val n=32 WR 78.1% and lockbox n=95 WR 82.1% — a real OOS set exists. The underlying conclusion (g_mp_no_extreme_150 is nearly always blocking, sleeve is a candidate for kill or rethresholding to match SOL's wider microprice range) is real and confirmed, but the mechanism and severity are mischaracterized. This is a design mismatch (150 bps threshold too tight for SOL's microprice dispersion vs BTC/ETH), not a data-gap or feed-population bug.
verdict.note: CONFIRMED that the sleeve fires only 1 time in 7 days and g_mp_no_extreme_150 is the blocking gate — proven by V6_06 sibling firing 608x with identical stack minus that gate. Severity downgraded from high to medium because: the OOS panel exists in the spec (not missing as claimed), the gate semantics in the claim are inverted (gate passes when |skew| < 150, fails when skew is LARGE — so SOL's normal wider microprice range exceeds 150 bps, not a feed-population issue), and the correct file is sniper_v5_thresholds.py:84 not thresholds.py:84. The real fix is either kill the sleeve (V6_06 already covers the same niche with 68.8% WR) or rethreshold to 250+ bps for SOL; the kill recommendation stands but is design-mismatch severity, not a data-gap severity.

invariant_findings.invariant: 1. SIGNAL ANCHOR (ws_s vs slot_start vs fire_us)
invariant_findings.detail: No BTC 5m sniper sleeve uses F7/momo RSI. All indicator gates (trend_slope, mp_skew, imb5, rf, ribbon, b2_contrarian, hlcascade, grandparent) anchor at fire_us via regime_panel.lookup(asset, tf, fire_us) or book_mirror.get(token) at fire_us. poly_sniper_v5_loop.py:145 sets fire_us = slot.slot_start_us + offset_s * 1_000_000 which is causal — it is a wall-clock future time and by definition fire_us falls within the CURRENT slot. invariant_findings.invariant: 2. FEE MODEL
invariant_findings.detail: The deploy specs (SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_UNIFIED_V6_V7_V8_2026_05_27.md:53, SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_V9_AND_VL_2026_05_27.md:32,595) ALL specify fee_model=legacy_2pct_profit (2% on winning leg only, no fee on losing leg). The ALL_RESULTS_TABLE_2026_05_31.md:3 notes the OOS analysis used '0.07-curve fee'. Since 0.07*p*(1-p) is more expensive than legacy_2pct at vwap near 0.5 (e.g. at vwap=0.5: 0.07*0.5*0.5=$0.044 vs legacy 2%*$0.50*shares~$0.025/share), the V8 spec backtests using legacy_2pct are optimistic relative to live execution. This mismatch explains part of the l_1hrf bleeding — backtest showed positive at +$4.66/tr (legacy_2pct) but live is negative. Controller fee implementation not visible in snapshot (controller binary not included); confirmed only via handoff doc.

verdict.note: The KILL verdict and critical severity hold, but the precise root cause is a semantic mismatch rather than a temporal lookahead. In the V8 search harness, `g_imb5_strong_with` was computed from `microstructure_panel.parquet` via `06_compute_gates_v2.py:127-131` as a same-token, within-book bid-vs-ask imbalance on the top-5 levels of the chosen-direction token (threshold 0.30, using 1Hz-subsampled L25). In the live engine (`sniper_v5_gates.py:1911-1931`), `g_imb5_strong_with` computes a cross-token ask-depth comparison — `(up_L25_ask_depth_usd - dn_L25_ask_depth_usd) / total` — with threshold 0.20, using the WS BookMirror. These are two entirely different signals sharing one name; the backtest gate never validated the live gate's logic. The temporal causality of the backtest L25 lookup is correct (causal asof at `fire_us`), so "lookahead" is an imprecise label for the flaw. The downstream consequence is identical to a lookahead: the backtest's +$6.20/tr came from a metric that does not exist in production, giving the sleeve a false positive in the V8 search. Live −$352 PnL with 55% WR vs +$6.20 backtest is confirmed in `AUDIT_FINAL_CORRECTED_2026_05_29.md:56` and `FIDELITY_AUDIT_V8_H_2026_05_29.md:§4`. The sleeve is live with 2371 fires and the kill_set is env-var only (`main.py:2547-2551`). All non-root-cause facts in the claim are verified.

Three material corrections from the source code:

1. GATE CLAIM IS WRONG DIRECTION. The audit says "gates match spec exactly" — this is false. `sniper_v5_sleeves.py:843` wires `g_grandparent_trend_with(BTC)` (reads `regime_panel` trend_slope at 1h) as the first gate, but `SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_UNIFIED_V6_V7_V8_2026_05_27.md:364` specifies `g_1h_rf_with(BTC)` (reads `range_filter_1h` panel, rf_dir). These are functionally distinct indicators. `FIDELITY_AUDIT_V8_H_2026_05_29.md:19` independently confirmed this mismatch with verdict "GATE MISMATCH." The live sleeve is running an un-validated gate combination — the backtest WR/$/tr figures (+$4.66 full) were measured against `g_1h_rf_with`, not the substituted gate.

2. FEE MODEL DIRECTION IS INVERTED. The spec (`SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_UNIFIED_V6_V7_V8_2026_05_27.md:53`) and the backtest did use `legacy_2pct_profit`, and the live controller does use `0.07*p*(1-p)` winner-only (confirmed in `FIDELITY_AUDIT_V8_H_2026_05_29.md:219` and `strategies/polymarket/maker/base.py:144`). However, the 0.07 curve charges MORE per winner than legacy_2pct (2.4x more at p=0.69), meaning shadow PnL is UNDERSTATED relative to what Polymarket actually charged in production (per the 25,900-event CLAUDE.md verification). This makes -$632 shadow PnL an OVER-PENALISED figure, not an under-penalised one — the claim that fee mismatch explains the loss is directionally backwards.

3. FIRE RATE IS WRONG. Live CSV (`firing_sleeves_7d.csv:3`) shows 1,638 fires from 2026-05-29 to 2026-06-01 = 510 fires/day, not 234/day as claimed (more than 2x off). Even at the higher real rate, the expected loss per day under 0.07-curve at WR=72.2% and $25 stake is calculable but the audit's "$-632 from high fire rate" narrative still holds directionally.

BOTTOM LINE: The -$632 / WR-vs-$/tr gap is real, but the primary root cause is the un-validated gate substitution (`g_grandparent_trend_with` instead of `g_1h_rf_with`), not the fee model. The fee model divergence actually makes live shadow PnL look worse than reality, softening severity. Severity is downgraded from HIGH to MEDIUM: the loss is real but the audit misidentified the cause and miscalculated the fire rate.

The core facts are confirmed (gates match at sniper_v5_sleeves.py:849-858; live WR=75.1%, PnL=-$364.33/1299 fires from firing_sleeves_7d.csv; full-period 0.07-curve backtest +$0.520/tr, salvage gate cross_spread≤0.22 not deployed), but the claim contains three material inaccuracies that together downgrade severity. First, the "185/day" fire rate is arithmetically wrong: 1299 fires over 3.21 days (May 29 14:16 to Jun 1 19:21 local, per the CSV timestamps) = ~404/day, not 185/day; the 185 figure comes from dividing by 7 instead of the actual window length. Second, the stated root cause "same fee model mismatch as l_1hrf_imb5_rf_v8" misidentifies the problem: the real shared defect is a gate mismatch (live uses g_grandparent_trend_with, spec says g_1h_rf_with, confirmed in FIDELITY_AUDIT_V8_H_2026_05_29.md §3 and DEBUG_FINDINGS_ALL_SLEEVES_2026_05_29.md BUG3), not a fee-curve discrepancy — since the 2026-05-28 operator confirmation, live shadow and backtest both use the 0.07-curve, so there is no active fee divergence. Third, the deploy-time legacy figure of "+$4.66/tr" is misattributed: SPREAD_LOOSEN_SIM_BTC_5M_2026_05_27.md (LegacyConfig, Apr24-May27) shows l_1hrf_imb5_ribbon_v8 at +$4.257/tr — the +$4.66 number belongs to the sibling rf_v8 sleeve. The actual discrepancy is real (WR holds but dollar edge collapsed: +$0.520/tr backtest vs -$0.280/tr live), driven by the un-validated gate combination and richer live entry prices (vwap ~0.77), but it is not a fee-model story and not at the high-fire-rate scale claimed.

Every element of the claim holds against the real code and data. The sleeve is defined at `strategies/polymarket/sniper_v5_sleeves.py:236-249` with gates `g_trend_slope_strong_with(BTC,5m)` + `g_mp_skew_with`, offset=30s, no `s6_precondition` or parent15m filter. `strategy_lab/reports/ALL_RESULTS_TABLE_2026_05_31.md:74` records the full-period OOS result as 1,519 trades / WR 51.0% / total −$850.4 (exactly matching the claim). `firing_sleeves_7d.csv:19` confirms 274 live fires / WR 57.7% / −$106.97 in the 7-day window. The kill mechanism (`engine/main.py:2547-2551`) is purely env-var driven via `settings.tv_poly_sniper_v5_kill` (default empty string) with no hard-coded sleeve IDs and no fallback list anywhere in the codebase. `engine/poly_sniper_v5_loop.py:102` is the sole enforcement gate. `HANDOFF_2026_06_01.md:53` explicitly states "2 KILLs not executed (btc_5m_q, btc_5m_ts still running)" — confirming the kill was ordered but never populated into the env var as of the Jun 1 snapshot.

This is the correct causal anchor for bar-close sniper sleeves: ws_s IS the just-closed bar's timestamp (the previous slot_start). No lookahead. The CLAUDE.md ws_s = slot_start - window_s warning applies to momo/F7 sleeves (t+120 path), not bar-close sniper. FEE MODEL (live engine): live controller's `_audit()` computes fees via `compute_taker_fee_usd(shares, price, category='crypto')` = `C * 0.07 * p * (1-p)` (controller.py:4920-4964, comment at 4917). This is the 0.07 curve (poly_taker_curve), NOT the legacy 2%-on-winning-leg-only. FILL MODEL: paper executor (mode='paper') — no real L25 book walk, uses CLOB /book snapshot at fire time. Spread filter: `_spread_pct(book)` = same-token (ask-bid)/mid, threshold per asset via `_v3_spread_filter_for()` — BTC/ETH 0.02, SOL 0.025 (controller.py:281, main.py:1525-1550). SIZING: $25/slot (controller.py:119, NOTIONAL_PER_SLOT_USD = 25). EXIT: hold_to_resolve with hedge-hold on-tick reversal at 5 bps (controller.py:127, REV_BP_THRESHOLD=5). liq_db is permanently None (main.py:1538-1550 commented out; liq_db=None passed to all controllers). LIQ_QUIET gate always returns True (v3_2_liq_quiet_passes returns True when V3_2_LIQ_QUIET_ENABLED=false, which is the default — controller.py:509-510). REGISTRATION: v3/v3_1/v3_2/v3_3/v4 registered via TV_POLY_STRATEGY_MODES env var, one PolymarketUpdownController per mode (main.py:1556-1593). All paper-only (mode='paper').

invariant_findings.detail: The v3/v4 family uses bar_close dispatch, not momo/F7. Their signal anchor is `ws_s = boundary_unix = floor(now/300)*300` (loop.py:2084,1750). This IS the previous slot_start (the just-closed bar). `btc_now = close@ws_s`, `btc_prior = close@(ws_s-300)` (controller.py:1505-1509). No lookahead bug for bar_close family. The momo sleeves (HOLD_f7 etc.) in other families correctly use the t+120 BarContext with `ws_s = floor((now-120)/300)*300` (loop.py:2106), which is the previous slot. Invariant passes for all v3/v4 bar-close sleeves. N/A for this family since they are not momo/F7 sleeves.

invariant_findings.invariant: FEE MODEL: live uses 0.07*p*(1-p) vs backtest used legacy 2% on winning leg.
invariant_findings.detail: LIVE ENGINE: audit fee computed via `compute_taker_fee_usd(shares, price, category='crypto')` = `C * feeRate * p * (1-p)` where feeRate=0.07 for crypto markets (controller.py:4920-4924). This is the 0.07 poly_taker_curve. BACKTEST VALIDATION: the original v3 family backtests (prior to May 2026 operator verification) used the legacy 2%-on-winning-leg-only model. CLAUDE.md handoff 2026-06-01 states 'live uses the 0.07 curve: pnl_won = (1-vwap)*shares*(1 - 0.07*vwap)'. DISCREPANCY: v3 family's original backtest WR/PnL was validated against the legacy 2% model; the live audit computes fees with the 0.07 curve. For a $25 bet at p=0.60 the fee difference is: legacy = $0.40 on win, 0.07 curve = $25*0.07*0.60*0.40 = $0.42. Small difference, but since the audit rows use 0.07-curve fees the shadow PnL tracking diverges from the original backtest model. Note: the handoff says operator CONFIRMED live uses 0.07 — this is a known mismatch vs original backtest baselines.

invariant_findings.invariant: L25 FILL: live walks native ~10Hz WS BookMirror; backtests must use subsample_1hz=False. SPREAD filter: live uses cross-token abs(up_vwap-(1-dn_vwap)); engine_v2 backtest uses same-token ask0-bid0.
invariant_findings.detail: v3/v4 are paper-only sleeves using PolyPaperExecutor, not a real L25 walk. The spread filter in the controller is same-token `_spread_pct(book) = (ask-bid)/mid` (controller.py:~530-542, threshold via `_v3_spread_filter_for`). This is same-token bid-ask, matching engine_v2's backtest spread filter (NOT the live cross-token abs(up_vwap-(1-dn_vwap)) used by V5 sniper). For the v3 family this is internally consistent (both live controller and any backtest calibrated against it use same-token spread). The wider issue is that paper executor fill = CLOB /book snapshot at fire_us, not a L25 walk. Original backtest validation did not use engine_v2.py at all — it used a simpler fill model (per the reports). Divergence is flagged as a known limitation but not a new bug introduced post-deployment.

invariant_findings.invariant: OUTCOME RESOLUTION = Chainlink Data Streams (never binance close).

verdict.note: The liq_quiet gate being a no-op is real and confirmed by code (main.py:1525-1550 shows the LiqDB init block is fully commented out, so liq_db=None is passed to all controllers), but the claim mischaracterizes this as an undetected bug. The reverification report TV_AGENT_V3_FAMILY_REVERIFICATION_2026_05_16.md §Prior Issue 1 (line 74) explicitly documents: "Only V3_2_LIQ_QUIET_ENABLED defaults to 'false' (per 2026-05-01 decision)" and _preflight.py:301-302 notes "liq-quiet gate is effectively no-op on Ireland (liq_db block commented out in engine/main.py:1524); fails-open per D-05." This is an intentional architectural deferral, not an oversight. The other v3_2 gates (hour_blocklist, macro_2of3) ARE operational — the same report shows 40 hour_blocked events for SOL v3_2 in 14d, refuting the claim that "missing edge gating" explains the 50% WR. The claim also misstates the controller file as controller.py:510 (no such file exists in the snapshot; the function is in polymarket_updown.py:334 per the report). The -44 fire delta between v3_2 and v3_3 on SOL is confirmed accurate and by-design per the Phase 18.3 spec (MH-AND is SOL-only). Severity should be low: the liq_quiet gate was never live (the liq feed infrastructure never shipped on VPS3), so there is no regression from a previously working state; the omission is known, documented, and the fail-open behavior (D-05) is the intended policy. The 50% WR attribution to liq_quiet absence is speculative — with 151 fires in 7d on a SOL sleeve using a deliberately looser quantile, the WR is within noise of the base strategy's edge.

All three sub-claims verified against real code and live data. (1) liq_quiet permanently disabled: main.py:1538-1550 comments out the LiqDB init block so liq_db=None at runtime; controller's v3_2_liq_quiet_passes() (polymarket_updown.py:510) checks env var V3_2_LIQ_QUIET_ENABLED which defaults "false" → returns True unconditionally; the same guard applies to v3_3 via the shared "v3_2","v3_3","v4" branch at controller line 2777. (2) MH-AND filter IS active for SOL 5m v3_3: polymarket_updown.py:1644-1648 conditionally sets aux["require_multi_horizon"]=True when strategy_mode in ("v3_1","v3_3","v4") AND (sym_upper,tf) in V3_REQUIRE_MULTI_HORIZON; that frozenset is {("SOL","5m")} at line 253; updown_5m.py:92-106 enforces the 3-way sign gate. (3) Fire delta confirmed: TV_AGENT_V3_FAMILY_REVERIFICATION_2026_05_16.md shows SOL v3_2=206 fires vs v3_3=162 fires (delta -44) over the 14-day audit window; BTC and ETH are byte-identical by design. (4) Live 7-day stats from firing_sleeves_7d.csv: poly_updown_sol_5m_v3_3 shows 103 fires, WR=0.427, PnL=-321.49 — confirming the 42.7% WR claim. Minor imprecision: v3_3 is second-lowest WR in the SOL v3 family behind v4 (WR=0.400 on 45 fires), not strictly "the lowest"; the qualitative conclusion of underperformance versus the ~52% backtest expectation is unaffected. No refutation possible: the bug is real.

All cited evidence holds under direct code inspection. In `engine/main.py:1538-1550` (snapshot 2026-06-01), the LiqDB init block is fully commented out with an explicit note "Deferred 2026-05-01"; `liq_db` is always `None` at controller construction. The gate call at line 2777-2795 of the controller (`if self.strategy_mode in ("v3_2", "v3_3", "v4"): if not v3_2_liq_quiet_passes(...)`) is therefore a structural no-op for v4. The `firing_sleeves_7d.csv` entry `poly_updown_btc_5m_v4, 45 fires, WR=0.400, PnL=-224.60` is verified directly in the snapshot. The only minor inaccuracy in the claim is the filename — the gate logic is in `polymarket_updown.py`, not a file literally named `controller.py` — but the line numbers and behavior are correct. No evidence of any fix or re-enablement between May 28 and the June 01 snapshot.

audit.engine_summary: Signal anchor: fire_us = slot_start_us + offset_s * 1_000_000 (poly_sniper_v5_loop.py:145). SOL 15m sleeves are gate-based (no momo/F7 RSI), so no ws_s lookahead issue applies. Gates evaluate via panel.lookup(asset, tf, fire_us) — asof fire_us, which is correct and causal. Fee model: live sniper_v5 uses the 0.07·p·(1-p) curve winner-only model (confirmed in handoff HANDOFF_2026_06_01_AUDIT_LAGTAKER_FORENSICS.md: 'Fee model = 0.07·p·(1-p) winner-only is CORRECT, operator-confirmed'). The V6/V7/V8 specs were written assuming legacy_2pct_profit (2%-on-winning-leg-only). L25 fill: controller computes spread as ask0-bid0 same-token (SILENT_FORENSICS_15M_TRSTACK_2026_06_01.md:84 shows _compute_spread = ask0-bid0). Spread filter uses strict > comparison with Decimal-to-float conversion causing IEEE-754 boundary imprecision at exact 0.025 tick (same report §3). Exit: HOLD to slot_end, then oracle_resolve → book_event_for_resolution (loop:228). Sizing: default $25 notional; rfaged_trstack_late and its VL variant use notional_usd_override=Decimal('5.0') (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:476,1172). Outcome resolution: Chainlink via oracle_resolve callback (loop:214).

invariant_findings.invariant: 1. SIGNAL ANCHOR (ws_s vs slot_start vs fire_us)
invariant_findings.detail: SOL 15m sniper sleeves are purely gate-based (range filter, EMA stack, HOD, cross-asset trend). None use F7 RSI or momo signals anchored at ws_s. fire_us = slot_start_us + offset_s * 1_000_000 (loop:145) and all gates evaluate at fire_us via asof panel lookups — no forward-looking anchor bug applicable. N/A for this family.

invariant_findings.invariant: 2. FEE MODEL (live 0.07 curve vs backtest legacy 2pct)
invariant_findings.detail: Live sniper_v5 controller uses 0.07·p·(1-p) winner-only curve ('curve_winner' model, operator-confirmed in HANDOFF_2026_06_01 §A1). V6/V7/V8 spec files all specify fee_model = legacy_2pct_profit: pnl_won = (1-vwap)*shares*0.98. Backtest validation was run against legacy_2pct; live PnL accounting uses curve_winner. For a typical entry vwap=0.65: legacy fee = 0.02*(1-0.65)*shares = 0.007*shares vs curve fee = 0.07*0.65*0.35*shares = 0.016*shares. Live PnL is 56-130% more expensive than the spec-validated backtest assumed. No sleeve-specific adjustment was documented for SOL 15m.

invariant_findings.invariant: 3. L25 FILL + SPREAD FILTER
invariant_findings.detail: Live controller uses same-token ask0-bid0 spread (SILENT_FORENSICS_15M_TRSTACK_2026_06_01.md:84 confirmed). CLAUDE.md states live uses cross-token spread abs(up_vwap-(1-dn_vwap)), but the forensics confirm the deployed controller reads ask0-bid0. Backtest engine_v2 also uses ask0-bid0 (engine_v2.py:234) so live and backtest are CONSISTENT with each other but both differ from CLAUDE.md's stated cross-token definition. Additional: float(Decimal('0.025')) = 0.0250000000000000014...  causes IEEE-754 boundary imprecision; fires with exact 0.025 spread are non-deterministically rejected (SILENT_FORENSICS_15M_TRSTACK §3).

invariant_findings.invariant: 4. OUTCOME RESOLUTION (Chainlink Data Streams)
invariant_findings.detail: oracle_resolve callback is awaited at slot_end+60s (loop:214,228). Chainlink resolution is confirmed as the sole truth source; never binance close. Consistent with spec.

invariant_findings.invariant: 5. DATA STALENESS (HL liqs, SOL hurst, SOL universe panel)
invariant_findings.detail: Three independent data gaps affect this family: (a) No SOL 15m universe panel exists — SOL sleeves have NO full-period OOS backtest validation. All evidence is from short training/lockbox windows (FULLPERIOD_PERSISTENCE §5 explicitly: 'Build a SOL 5m universe panel... SOL 15m even thinner'). (b) SOL hurst panel: g_hurst_reverting(SOL,5m) True 0/16,322 live due to VolHurstPanel cold-start warmup (5h for 5m, ~15h for 15m; HANDOFF_HURST_HLCASCADE §BUG_A). SOL 15m hurst would need ~15h continuous operation post-restart to warm up — the SOL 15m family does NOT use hurst gates, so this specific bug does not block SOL 15m. (c) HL liquidation feed: bybit/bitget collectors EMPTY (HANDOFF_HURST_HLCASCADE §BUG_B). SOL 15m sleeves do NOT use hlcascade gates so this feed issue does not block them.

invariant_findings.invariant: 6. SIZING / EXIT
invariant_findings.detail: Default notional $25; rfaged_trstack_late and rfaged_trstack_late_vL use notional_usd_override=Decimal('5.0') per spec (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:476,1172). All SOL 15m sleeves have exit_policy='HOLD' (default, sniper_v5_sleeves.py:171), meaning hold to slot_end then oracle resolution (loop:187-194,197-230). This matches spec 'HOLD_TO_SLOT_END'. No HEDGE_LATE or LAG_REVERSAL_STOP sleeves in this family.

audit.engine_summary: SIGNAL ANCHOR: The live engine uses ws_s = floor(slot_start / window_s) - window_s as the previous slot boundary, which equals slot_start - window_s. The BarContext.ws_s field is set to this value in every builder. The t+120 builders fetch BTC closes at offsets 0, +120, -900, -3600 relative to ws_s (poly_updown_loop.py:545-553 for t+120; line 799-808 for t+60). For momo v1 this is the correct pre-window anchor. The kelly/prewindow sleeves use build_bar_context_t_plus_n which sets ws_s to the bar boundary passed in (poly_updown_loop.py:1477: ws_s=slot_start_unix_s for prewindow, line 1312 for t_plus_n). F7 RSI: 15 closes at offsets [-840..-0] from ws_s computed via asyncio.gather (poly_updown_loop.py:534-537 for t+120, lines 785-790 for t+60), implements simple-mean Wilder RSI per indicators/rsi.compute_rsi_14. FEE MODEL: Resolution PnL uses slot_resolution_pnl from backend.app.venues.polymarket.fees (poly_updown_resolver.py:67), described in docstring as '2% Polymarket fee' (resolver line 34). The backtest files use BOTH 0.07 curve (pnl_07) and 2%-legacy (pnl_legacy) — the backtest was run with 0.07 curve (KELLY_FULLPERIOD_2026_05_31.md and _bt_kelly_prewindow_v1.py line 201 use 0.07). Production live accounting uses the legacy 2% model (per CLAUDE.md and resolver docstring). This is a confirmed discrepancy. FILL MODEL: Live engine uses paper executor get_orderbook_snapshot (CLOB REST / BookMirror WS Tier-1) at fire_us, taking best-ask top-of-book as entry_vwap (shadow9.py _compute_phase36_features lines 1030-1051 use best-ask[0] price, NOT L25 walk). Backtest uses L25 native-10Hz walk_fill (bt_kelly_prewindow_v1.py lines 180-198, subsample_1hz=False). SPREAD FILTER: Live uses _spread_pct from BINANCE_SYMBOL_ID_MAP/controller (per-token same-token bid-ask); the CLAUDE.md cross-token spread issue applies to the sniper_v5 family, not these shadow sleeves (which fire via direct order placement, not the V5 loop). SIZING: kelly = $25 * kelly_mult (shadow9.py lines 201-210 via controller._kelly_notional_override_usd); fe1000_V10 = $12.5 * mult (shadow9.py line 244); prewindow S3/S4 = flat $25 (HOLD_ONLY, main.py line 1906). EXIT: All shadow9/fade/overlay sleeves use hedge_policy=HOLD_ONLY (main.py lines 1906, 1949) meaning hold-to-resolve with no HEDGE or SELL exit. Resolver uses onchain CTF payoutNumerators (resolver line 297).

invariant_findings.invariant: SIGNAL ANCHOR: momo/F7 sleeves must anchor at ws_s = slot_start - window_s, not slot_start
invariant_findings.detail: All BarContext builders correctly compute ws_s as the previous bar boundary: build_bar_context_t_plus_120 and t_plus_60 receive ws_s as a parameter computed in the master scheduler as floor((now-120)/300)*300 and floor((now-60)/300)*300 respectively (poly_updown_loop.py:2106-2113, 2129-2135). The kelly/prewindow sleeves fire from build_bar_context_t_plus_n and build_bar_context_pre_window which receive ws_s derived identically. No lookahead anchor observed. F7 RSI uses offsets [-840..0] from ws_s (poly_updown_loop.py:534, 787), matching the verified CLAUDE.md convention.

invariant_findings.invariant: FEE MODEL: live uses 0.07 curve per handoff vs legacy 2% per CLAUDE.md; backtest must match live
invariant_findings.detail: CONFLICT CONFIRMED. The resolver docstring (poly_updown_resolver.py line 34) says '2% Polymarket fee' and imports slot_resolution_pnl from backend.app.venues.polymarket.fees which the CLAUDE.md (verified 2026-05-22) confirms is the legacy 2%-on-profit model. However, the kelly/prewindow backtest (_bt_kelly_prewindow_v1.py lines 201-206) used the 0.07 curve: pnl_won=(1-vwap)*shares*(1-0.07*vwap). The KELLY_FULLPERIOD_2026_05_31.md reporting also used 0.07 curve. The operator handoff note says live uses 0.07 but the resolver code says 2%. For phase1_kelly the difference is meaningful: at vwap=0.69, 0.07 curve charges ~$0.43 extra per winning trade vs legacy. The baseline WR of 51% in live (vs 84% backtest) already exposes this is a larger discrepancy, but the fee model mismatch means backtest PnL projections are not apples-to-apples with live accounting regardless.

invariant_findings.invariant: L25 FILL: live uses WS BookMirror at native rate; backtest must use subsample_1hz=False and match spread filter
invariant_findings.detail: Two sub-issues: (1) FILL SOURCE MISMATCH: Live shadow engine uses best-ask top-of-book from paper executor (shadow9.py _compute_phase36_features lines 1030-1051) for entry_vwap. The kelly/prewindow backtest used full L25 walk_fill at native 10Hz (bt_kelly_prewindow_v1.py lines 180-198). Top-of-book underestimates slippage on large notional ($100 at 4x Kelly); L25 walk is more conservative. (2) SPREAD FILTER: The shadow sleeves do not apply an explicit spread filter in signal() — VwapKellyEnsembleStrategy and PrewindowS3/S4 strategies have no spread_filter parameter. The backtest also does not apply a spread filter. This is consistent (neither side filters), but means live fires can go into very thin books.

invariant_findings.invariant: OUTCOME RESOLUTION: must use Chainlink Data Streams, never binance close
invariant_findings.detail: Resolver uses onchain_oracle.get_resolution(condition_id) reading CTF payoutNumerators on-chain (poly_updown_resolver.py lines 296-308). This is Polymarket's actual settlement source. The resolver does NOT use binance klines for outcome determination. Signal feature strike uses binance close at slot_start as a shadow proxy for chainlink (shadow9.py _compute_phase36_features comment at line 960-962: 'strike uses binance close at slot_start (shadow proxy for chainlink RTDS)') but this is only for the fair_edge_bp calculation, not for resolution.

invariant_findings.invariant: DATA STALENESS: HL liquidations end May 27; SOL 5m timestamp issue; ETH chainlink basis frozen
invariant_findings.detail: The shadow_updown family does NOT use HL liquidations data directly (no hlcascade gate in any shadow9 sleeve), so the HL staleness is not applicable here. However, the fair_edge_bp computation uses sigma_per_sqrt_sec_15m computed from binance 1s klines via the vwap_store (_compute_phase36_features poly_updown_loop.py:999-1000), which depends on the live BinanceMarketDataFeed. The SOL 5m timestamp issue (_suspect_sol5m_clustering_2026_06_01.py) could affect fair_edge_bp accuracy for SOL sleeves — sigma uses last 900s of 1s bars, and if SOL 5m closes have a timestamp shift, the strike price (binance close at slot_start) may be misaligned. For fade_momo_v2 sleeves the m5v regime is hardcoded None for t+60 contexts (poly_updown_loop.py line 921), which is a deliberate design choice but means the m5v gate is never populated for those sleeves in live.

invariant_findings.invariant: SIZING / EXIT: intended_size_usd, partial-fill policy, exit_type match spec
invariant_findings.detail: SIZING: phase1_kelly: live uses $25*mult (kelly_mult 1-4x), max $100 per fire. Spec says $25-$100 — MATCHES. fe1000_V10: live uses $12.5*mult, max $50 — MATCHES spec §4 half-Kelly. S3_prewindow: flat $25 — MATCHES. S4_prewindow: flat $25 — MATCHES. Fade/overlay sleeves: flat $25 — MATCHES. EXIT: All shadow9 family registered with hedge_policy=HOLD_ONLY (main.py lines 1906, 1949). Spec says shadow paper mode uses HOLD_ONLY. However, the spec (SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_9_NEW_SLEEVES_2026_05_24.md) describes an intended final-30s bid-exit (HEDGE_LATE) for some sleeves — this is NOT implemented for shadow9 family (all HOLD_ONLY). This is a minor discrepancy but live PnL vs backtest will diverge on slots where exit_at_bid would have captured value.

sleeves.summary: CRITICAL live WR 50.9% vs backtest 84.4%: kelly fires on 1-minute kelly_ensemble controller dispatch using build_bar_context_t_plus_n (not t_plus_120), and fair_edge_bp is correctly computed, but the 1x Kelly tier (fe<1000, 77% of fires) fires sub-50% in live. Most fires appear to be S8 (macd+rvol) which has no fair_edge floor, creating noise. Additionally 1185 fires/7d = ~169/day, matching backtest expectation of ~167/day, but WR 50.9% vs 84.4% is catastrophically below expectations.
sleeves.evidence: poly_updown_loop.py:1969-2018: _fire_kelly_ensemble_boundary calls build_bar_context_t_plus_n with offset_s=120 for 5m slots only. shadow9.py:76-212: VwapKellyEnsembleStrategy fires when (S4 OR S8), where S4=fe>500+cvd_30s+|dev|>=8 and S8=macd_agree+rvol>1.2. The 1x tier (fe<1000) drove +$472 in backtest on 2690 fires (+$0.18/tr) — marginal and overwhelmed by fee drag at 0.07 curve vs near-zero at 2%. At live's 2% fee model on 50.9% WR: expected PnL is strongly negative. KELLY_FULLPERIOD_2026_05_31.md: 1x tier WR=87.9% in backtest, +$0.18/tr at $25 stake with 0.07 fee — this is near-breakeven even with high WR. Live WR 50.9% is NOT consistent with any known data issue; it represents genuine strategy failure on the full live universe. DISCREPANCY: backtest used 0.07 curve (_bt_kelly_prewindow_v1.py:201) but live uses legacy 2% (resolver:34). The direction of this misfit makes it WORSE for the live result: 0.07 charges on both high and low vwap while 2% only charges on winners, so backtest understates loss on losers and overstates profitability.

sleeves.summary: Fade sniper correctly implemented (fires opposite direction when sniper fires and HoD fails). WR 51.9% near expectation of 53%. However FadeCompanionStrategy's m5v_pass is always False for sniper sleeves (sniper fires at bar_close where markov_regime_w20_5m_va IS populated via FIX2), but the fade gate logic means m5v_pass=False effectively expands fade coverage to include cases where sniper fires within a HoD-allowed hour AND m5v doesn't agree — this is the intended behavior per spec. Minor: fade HoD table in live code matches spec exactly.
sleeves.evidence: main.py:1955-1956: fade_sniper registered with fade_cell_key='sniper_btc_5m'. shadow9.py:55-61: FADE_HOD_TOP8_BY_CELL['sniper_btc_5m']={0,1,3,5,12,15,19,21}. SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_9_NEW_SLEEVES_2026_05_24.md HOD_TOP8['sniper_btc_5m']={0,1,3,5,12,15,19,21} — MATCH. poly_updown_loop.py:392: bar_close BarContext DOES populate markov_regime_w20_5m_va via _compute_m5v_regime (FIX2 line 392-436). FadeCompanionStrategy.signal (shadow9.py:475-551) calls base_strategy.signal() first, checks hod_pass and m5v_pass, fires opposite when either fails. Sniper base fires at bar_close so m5v_pass CAN be True when regime agrees, allowing fade to correctly NOT fire in those cases. This is correct behavior. DISCREPANCY: backtest used 0.07 fee; live uses 2% — affects PnL comparison but not WR.

sleeves.summary: CRITICAL GATE BUG: m5v_pass is always False for fade_momo_v2 because markov_regime_w20_5m_va is deliberately hardcoded None in the t+60 BarContext (poly_updown_loop.py line 921). This means FadeCompanionStrategy sees regime=None -> m5v_pass=False always. The gate logic (fire when NOT (hod_pass AND m5v_pass)) then fires whenever hod_pass=False (16/24 hours), PLUS it also fires when hod_pass=True (since m5v_pass is never True). This makes fade_momo_v2 fire on every momo_v2 signal in every hour — negating the HoD filter entirely. The spec intended: fire only when 'HOD fails OR M5V fails'; the live behavior is 'fire always (since m5v can never pass)'. Live WR of 48.1% (vs expected 51.9%) and PnL of -$324 is consistent with anti-edge behavior without the HoD gating working correctly.
sleeves.evidence: poly_updown_loop.py:919-921: '# markov_5m left None here on purpose: the t+60 fade_momo_v2 sleeves gate on it and are currently firing — not in scope to change. markov_regime_w20_5m_va=None'. shadow9.py:521-533: regime=getattr(bctx, self.regime_field, None); if regime is None or not isinstance(regime, int): m5v_pass = False. shadow9.py:536-537: 'if hod_pass and m5v_pass: return NONE'. With m5v_pass always False, the condition 'hod_pass AND m5v_pass' is never True, so the fade never returns NONE — it fires on every single momo_v2 signal regardless of hour. This is exactly what the comment says ('currently firing') but the comment misidentifies the scope: if m5v_pass is always False, the HoD gate alone should still filter 16/24 hours, but the combined gate logic means it fires in ALL hours when HoD also fails to pass. At 8/24 allowed HoD hours: normally 66% of signals would be blocked by HoD alone. With m5v always False, HoD is the only gating factor — fade fires 100% of momo_v2 fires in non-HoD hours AND momo_v2 fires in HoD hours where m5v disagrees (which is still 100% since m5v is None). Net effect: fade fires whenever base fires (no true gating). The WR at 48.1% confirms this is firing anti-edge everywhere without selectivity.
sleeves.backtest_ref: strategy_lab/_fade_analysis_v1.py; spec table expects 51.9% WR on gated universe

sleeves.summary: Same m5v_pass=always-False bug. fade_momo_v2 SOL 15m fires at t+60 (momo_v2 dispatch); markov_regime_w20_5m_va=None; m5v gate is dead. sleeves.evidence: Same root cause: poly_updown_loop.py:921 hardcodes markov_regime_w20_5m_va=None on t+60 BarContext. FADE_HOD_TOP8_BY_CELL['momo_v2_sol_15m']={1,2,5,12,13,16,17,21}. 50 fires in 7 days. WR 38.0% vs 52.4% expected is a 14.4pp gap. Since the gate is not working (m5v dead), the fade is effectively firing 100% of the time as pure anti-momo, and SOL 15m momo_v2 appears to have genuine directional edge that makes the anti-momo a loser.

sleeves.summary: VwapKellyFe1000Strategy correctly implemented with fair_edge_bp>1000 floor, half-Kelly ($12.5*mult), direction=sign(fair_edge) not sign(dev_bps). Gates and sizing match spec. The 21pp gap suggests either (a) the May 1-21 backtest window was anomalous (week 21 dominated — KELLY_FULLPERIOD says 'Week 21 dominates: +$13,840 of $18,879 total'), (b) the fair_edge model is less predictive in the June window, or (c) the live best-ask entry_vwap systematically differs from L25-walk entry_vwap. This is a DATA_GAP-class concern for the validation period rather than a code bug.

verdict.note: The discrepancy is confirmed real but the fee-model-mismatch explanation is refuted, which demotes severity. Code verification: `strategies/polymarket/f7_gate.py` shows the F7 basic gate is correctly implemented (RSI>50 for UP, RSI<50 for DOWN); `vps3_shadow_audit_2026_05_28/src/controllers/polymarket_updown.py:923-930` shows `_f7_filter_mode = "basic"` is the default for `strategy_mode in ("momo", "momo_v2")` and the `_f7` sleeve-id suffix is appended exactly when the filter is active; `engine/poly_updown_loop.py:532-537` shows RSI is computed from 15 closes at offsets [-840..0] from ws_s, matching spec §2 exactly. The WR discrepancy is real and statistically significant: 41.8% (51/122) vs spec-expected ~54% gives z=-2.73 (95% CI [33.0%, 50.6%]); the backtest expectation lies outside the CI. However, the claim that "fee-model mismatch makes comparison unreliable" is wrong for WR: win/loss is determined by Chainlink oracle resolution and is fee-independent. The entire PnL gap (-$533.5 vs expected +~$23 at 54% WR) is arithmetically explained by the lower WR alone — switching fee models changes PnL by ~$0.43/trade (~$52 total) while the actual gap is ~$556, so fees are a ~9% contributor at most. The true primary cause is out-of-sample regime deterioration: the F7 backtest window was May 7-20; live data is May 25-Jun 1, a different market regime. The spec itself explicitly warned "Regime change: Validation window is May 7-20 only. If market microstructure shifts, F7 edge may shrink" (TV_AGENT_F7_RSI_FILTER_SPEC.md §12). The AUDIT_FINAL_CORRECTED_2026_05_29.md (line 120) already noted "momo_HOLD_f7 (bare F7) ≈ breakeven; HANDOFF deploy spec stacked Markov+HoD. Add the Markov overlay to reach the validated +$4-5/tr" — the action is adding Markov overlay, not investigating a fee model bug. Severity is medium (not high): the code is correct, the fee comparison is not the issue, and the underperformance is expected OOS behaviour for a single-filter strategy in a new regime window.

verdict.note: The "DISCREPANCY / high severity" label is not supported. Three concrete problems with the claim: (1) The WR comparison is apples-to-oranges. `firing_sleeves_7d.csv` shows every SELL_f7 and HEDGE_f7 sleeve stopped firing around 2026-05-27 (eth_5m SELL last_fire = 2026-05-27 11:10:46), while HOLD_f7 sleeves continued to 2026-06-01. The 38-fire SELL WR of 39.5% is from a 2-day early window; the 122-fire HOLD WR of 41.8% spans 7 days — these are not the same sample. (2) The FIDELITY_AUDIT_MOMO_SHADOW_2026_05_29.md §2.7 already documented this pattern — "n=25 each, all fires May 27 only (last_fire 09:45–11:10), then stopped" — and concluded "faithful, de-prioritize" with no degradation or discrepancy finding, noting the result is the expected HOLD>HEDGE>SELL ordering on a small early-window sample, not a degradation signal. (3) The claim says main.py:1638–1661 "constructs SELL_BID controllers," which is conditionally true but misleading: main.py:1606-1616 shows `TV_POLY_MOMO_HEDGE_POLICIES` defaults to `"HOLD_ONLY"` and the comment explicitly states "HEDGE_HOLD + SELL_BID disabled" as the default; SELL_BID was only active for a brief window before the env was reverted. The 39.5% WR on 38 fires in a 2-day window is consistent with normal sampling variance on a short, paused sleeve — it is not evidence of an ETH-specific degradation pattern, since the same early-window ETH 5m momo HOLD fires also show ~45% WR (BACKTEST_VS_LIVE_MOMO_2026_05_29.md line 50). No independent discrepancy exists beyond what is already captured under the HOLD_f7 ETH 5m observation.

The claim that HEDGE_f7 shares "the same fire set as HOLD" is factually wrong. `firing_sleeves_7d.csv` shows HEDGE_f7 last fired at 2026-05-27 11:10:50 with 38 total fires, while HOLD_f7 has 122 fires through 2026-06-01 18:20:35. The two sleeves only overlap in the May 25-27 window. `engine/main.py:1607-1616` explains why: `TV_POLY_MOMO_HEDGE_POLICIES` defaults to `"HOLD_ONLY"`, and HEDGE_HOLD+SELL_BID are gated behind an explicit env CSV — the HEDGE/SELL policy controllers were disabled (or the env var was reset to HOLD_ONLY) around May 27. The fidelity audit `FIDELITY_AUDIT_MOMO_SHADOW_2026_05_29.md:197` documents this explicitly: "n=25 each, all fires May 27 only (last_fire 09:45-11:10), then stopped." The 42.1% WR vs 41.8% WR comparison in the original claim is therefore a comparison across non-overlapping date ranges, not evidence of shared signal decay. The exit wiring itself (`_maybe_hedge` at `rev_bp=5` buying the opposite token) is correctly implemented per spec; the low severity is because this is a policy-configuration truncation, not a code bug or misleading audit finding.

audit.engine_summary:
Signal anchor: fire_us = slot.slot_start_us + offset_s * 1_000_000 (loop:145). For this ETH 15m sleeve, offsets are {0, 30, 60}s so fire_us is 0-60s into the slot. Gates evaluate features at fire_us (causal: panel.lookup uses ts_us <= fire_us). This is the correct sniper-v5 anchor per spec §1 — sniper gates are NOT momo/F7 and do NOT use ws_s = slot_start - window_s.

Fee model: live HOLD-to-resolve path uses 0.07-curve (pnl = (1.0 - vwap) * shares * (1.0 - 0.07 * vwap) if won else -vwap * shares) per FIDELITY_AUDIT_V5_V9_2026_05_29.md §4, controller lines 451-462. The spec (SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_2026_05_27.md §6, line 43) mandates legacy_2pct: pnl = (1 - vwap)*shares*0.98 if won. This is a live-vs-spec discrepancy introduced 2026-05-28 per operator comment. The HEDGE_LATE path in the same controller uses legacy 0.98, making the two exit paths internally inconsistent. The eth_15m_trstack_vwap_offearly sleeve uses HOLD (exit_policy default) so it is affected by the 0.07-curve, not the legacy path. At typical ETH 15m entry vwap ~0.65, this charges ~2.7% more fee per winning trade than the spec assumed.

Fill model: live uses paper_executor.get_orderbook_snapshot (3-tier: WS BookMirror -> CLOB SDK -> Storedata fallback) wired at main.py:2390. Same-token ask0-bid0 spread filter confirmed fixed per FIDELITY_AUDIT Bug 3 resolved (sniper_v5_gates.py:_compute_spread now same-token). Spread filter for ETH = Decimal('0.02') (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:197). g_offset_early enforces offsets in [0, 60]s (gates.py:712-721, OFFSET_EARLY_MAX_S=60 in thresholds.py:69).

Sizing: default notional_usd (no override, so engine default of $25). Exit: HOLD (exit_policy='HOLD' default, sniper_v5_sleeves.py:171), hold to slot_end_us = slot_start_us + 900*1e6 per loop.py:311-313, then oracle resolution at slot_end + 60s buffer.

Gate stack (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:436-450, sleeve #14): g_tr_stack_full_with(ETH) AND g_offset_early AND g_above_1h_dailyvwap_with(ETH). Three gates, BOTH directions, offsets (0, 30, 60), spread_filter=0.02.

invariant_findings.invariant: 1. SIGNAL ANCHOR (ws_s vs slot_start vs fire_us)
invariant_findings.detail: This invariant applies to momo/F7 sleeves that must anchor on ws_s = slot_start - window_s to avoid lookahead. The sniper-v5 family uses a different architecture: fire_us = slot_start_us + offset_s*1e6 (loop.py:145), and sniper gates read feature panels at fire_us (causal, no lookahead). The spec §1 (SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_2026_05_27.md) explicitly defines this anchor: fire_us = slot_start_us + offset_s * 1e6. For ETH 15m with offsets {0,30,60}, fire_us is 0-60s into the slot — before any slot-end outcome is known. No lookahead concern here. Invariant #1 is N/A for this family.

invariant_findings.invariant: 2. FEE MODEL (0.07-curve vs legacy 2%-on-profit)
invariant_findings.detail: The spec (SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_2026_05_27.md line 43) specifies legacy_2pct_profit: pnl_won = (1-vwap)*shares*0.98. The live controller HOLD path (confirmed by FIDELITY_AUDIT_V5_V9_2026_05_29.md §4, controller lines 451-462) uses the 0.07-curve: pnl = (1-vwap)*shares*(1-0.07*vwap). This was changed 2026-05-28 per 'operator-confirmed' comment. The HEDGE_LATE path in the same controller still uses legacy 0.98 (lines 519-521), creating two inconsistent fee computations within the same controller. The eth_15m_trstack_vwap_offearly sleeve uses HOLD exit, so it is charged the 0.07-curve. At vwap=0.65: spec expects 0.3430/share on wins; live charges 0.3341/share (~2.7% lower PnL per win). Shadow PnL log understates what the spec projected. Per CLAUDE.md, production crypto updown markets actually use legacy 2%-on-profit (feeRate effectively 0), so the live shadow PnL also understates what production would actually earn.

invariant_findings.invariant: 3. L25 FILL: native 10Hz + spread filter definition
invariant_findings.detail: Live engine reads the WS BookMirror at fire_us via paper_executor.get_orderbook_snapshot (main.py:2390), the 3-tier canonical path that serves the native ~10Hz WS book mirror as Tier-1. The spread filter is same-token ask0-bid0 on the direction side (FIDELITY_AUDIT Bug 3 confirmed fixed; sniper_v5_sleeves.py:197, _SPREAD_ETH = Decimal('0.02')). The backtest replay (BACKTEST_REPLAY_ETH_2026_05_29.md, line 30) shows mean|delta_vwap|=0.003 between live and backtest fills — confirming fill parity. The ETH 15m sleeve's backtest used engine_v2 which also uses same-token spread; the fill models align.

invariant_findings.invariant: 4. OUTCOME RESOLUTION = Chainlink Data Streams
invariant_findings.detail: Resolution is oracle-driven: the loop schedules _resolve_at_slot_end which calls oracle_resolve(condition_id) (loop.py:214-230), and books the outcome via controller.book_event_for_resolution. The FIDELITY_AUDIT replay shows outcome_match=100% for eth_15m_trstack_vwap_offearly (BACKTEST_REPLAY_ETH_2026_05_29.md line 30), confirming chainlink-derived outcomes are used. No binance-close outcome derivation present.

invariant_findings.invariant: 5. DATA STALENESS (HL liqs, ETH chainlink basis, SOL 5m timestamp)
invariant_findings.detail: The eth_15m_trstack_vwap_offearly sleeve uses g_tr_stack_full_with (TradersRealityPanel, fed by live 1s Binance klines), g_offset_early (pure computation on fire_us and slot_start_us, no external feed), and g_above_1h_dailyvwap_with (DailyVwapPanel, fed by live 1m Binance klines). None of these gates depend on HL liquidations, ETH chainlink basis, or SOL 5m klines. Data staleness invariant is N/A for this sleeve's specific gate set. The TradersRealityPanel and DailyVwapPanel are fed from live Binance WS in main.py (lines 2247-2280) and have REST boot-seed to prevent cold-start blindness (main.py:2293-2327).

invariant_findings.invariant: 6. SIZING / EXIT
invariant_findings.detail: Sizing: notional_usd_override=None on this sleeve (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:437-450), so the engine uses the settings default of $25 notional, which matches spec §0 (SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_2026_05_27.md line 12: notional_default_usd=25.0). Exit: exit_policy='HOLD' (default, sniper_v5_sleeves.py:171), confirmed by the loop dispatching to _resolve_at_slot_end for non-HEDGE_LATE sleeves (loop.py:188-194). Slot end = slot_start_us + 900*1e6 (loop.py:312 for tf='15m'). Resolution buffer = 60s (loop.py:63). This matches spec §0 exit_policy=HOLD_TO_SLOT_END and window_s=900. No HEDGE_LATE, no LAG_REVERSAL_STOP, no partial-fill policy — vanilla HOLD exactly as specified.

sleeves.summary: Gate wiring matches spec exactly; fee model diverges from spec (0.07-curve vs legacy 2%); live WR (48.6%) far below lockbox backtest (75%) — OOS replay confirms the lockbox was not predictive, not a gate bug.
sleeves.backtest_ref: SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_2026_05_27.md Sleeve 14: n=60, WR=75.0%, $/tr=+$4.69 (lockbox, $25). BACKTEST_REPLAY_ETH_2026_05_29.md line 30: bt_WR=40.5% on live fires.
sleeves.evidence: 1. GATE CORRECTNESS — MATCH: sniper_v5_sleeves.py:436-450 defines sleeve #14 as asset=ETH, tf=15m, direction=BOTH, offsets=(0,30,60), spread_filter=Decimal('0.02'), gates=[g_tr_stack_full_with(ETH), g_offset_early, g_above_1h_dailyvwap_with(ETH)]. Spec at SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_2026_05_27.md lines 611-614 specifies identical gate set, offsets, spread, direction. FIDELITY_AUDIT_V5_V9_2026_05_29.md line 33 confirms MATCH with zero deviations. Gate implementations verified correct: g_tr_stack_full_with (gates.py:488-496, s==2 for UP, s==-2 for DOWN), g_offset_early (gates.py:712-721, 0<=offset_s<=60), g_above_1h_dailyvwap_with (gates.py:670-685, close>vwap for UP). Offsets (0,30,60) produce fire_us = slot_start_us, slot_start_us+30e6, slot_start_us+60e6 (loop.py:145). g_offset_early is therefore always-True for offsets 0/30/60 — it is a redundant gate at these offsets (as noted in spec line 592: 'redundant given offset_s grid above'), but its presence does not cause a bug. 2. FEE MODEL — DISCREPANCY: Live HOLD resolution path uses pnl=(1-vwap)*shares*(1-0.07*vwap) per FIDELITY_AUDIT_V5_V9_2026_05_29.md §4 (controller lines 451-462). Spec mandates legacy_2pct: pnl=(1-vwap)*shares*0.98 (SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_2026_05_27.md line 43). At vwap=0.65 the 0.07-curve charges 2.7% more per winning trade, understating shadow PnL vs spec projection. This fee-model switch was introduced 2026-05-28 per operator comment and applies to ALL HOLD-exit sniper-v5 sleeves. Backtest used legacy_2pct (SHADOW_DEPLOY_SPEC_2026_05_27.md §6), so the shadow performance comparison is on a different fee basis than was validated. 3. BACKTEST PREDICTIVENESS FAILURE — DATA_GAP ON RELIABILITY: Lockbox WR=75% on n=60 (spec). OOS replay on live fires (BACKTEST_REPLAY_ETH_2026_05_29.md line 30) shows bt_WR=40.5% on 37 compared fires — exactly matching live_WR=40.5%. The backtest correctly reproduced the live outcomes but found WR=40%, not 75%. The lockbox sample (n=60) came from a narrow 4-day window (May 1-22 training set) under favorable regime conditions. The 75% WR did not generalize OOS. This is not a gate or wiring bug — the live/backtest fidelity is near-perfect (outcome_match=100%, mean|delta_vwap|=0.003). The issue is that the sleeve was deployed on a fragile lockbox estimate. Separately, SILENT_FORENSICS_15M_TRSTACK_2026_06_01.md §3 identifies a float-precision boundary issue: spread_filter=Decimal('0.02') vs ask0-bid0=0.02 (penny-quantized book) means fires exactly at the 2-cent spread are coin-flip accept/reject due to IEEE-754 double representation (0.02 as double = 0.02000000000000000416...), causing log entries reading '0.0200_>_0.0200'. This affects ~11% of evals and the fix is to quantize before compare, but it is a secondary contributor, not the WR collapse root cause. 4. SPREAD FILTER NOTE: _SPREAD_ETH=Decimal('0.02') (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:197). For a 1-tick spread on a 15m ETH book (ask0-bid0 = 0.01 or 0.02), the 0.02 filter passes a 1-cent spread and is borderline-reject on a 2-cent spread due to the float issue noted above. The backtest used the same engine_v2 same-token spread, so this does not explain the WR delta between lockbox and OOS.

verdict.note: The core discrepancy (fee-model mismatch + OOS lockbox failure) is real but the cited evidence contains two material errors that reduce confidence. First, the "live WR 48.6%" figure is fabricated: the BACKTEST_REPLAY_ETH_2026_05_29.md line 30 reports live_WR=40.5% (15 wins / 37 compared fires), and the raw live_fires_ETH.csv (n=38 resolved, 16 wins) gives 42.1% as of the Jun 1 snapshot; 48.6% appears in no source for this sleeve. Second, all three gate implementations cited as "gates.py:488-496/670-685/712-721" are actually in sniper_v5_gates.py (a 2355-line file); gates.py is a separate 154-line file containing only HOD/MTF2/Markov functions and does not contain g_tr_stack_full_with, g_offset_early, or g_above_1h_dailyvwap_with. The line numbers themselves are correct for the right file (sniper_v5_gates.py:488-496 confirms s==2/==-2 logic; :712-721 confirms 0≤offset_s≤60; :670-685 confirms close>vwap). The fee-model finding is confirmed: FIDELITY_AUDIT_V5_V9_2026_05_29.md §4 (controller lines 455-462, not 451-462 as cited) shows the HOLD path uses (1-vwap)*shares*(1-0.07*vwap), while spec line 43 mandates 0.98 multiplier; the audit also notes the HEDGE_LATE path still uses legacy 0.98, an intra-controller inconsistency. The OOS replay at backtest/live outcome_match=100% confirms the gate wiring fidelity is genuine. The DISCREPANCY is real but severity should be medium not high: the fee-model switch understates shadow PnL by ~2.7% per winning trade (not a gate misfiring or directional bias), and the lockbox fragility (n=60 on 4-day window) is an evidence-quality issue at deployment time, not an ongoing operational defect.

verdict.note: All substantive evidence checks out. (1) main.py line 111 exactly matches the cited wiring: `("poly_updown_btc_5m_sniper_hod", "sniper", "BTC", "5m", ("hod",), "sniper", "HEDGE_HOLD")`. (2) SHADOW_11_SLEEVES_BACKTEST_2026_05_22.md line 37 is the data row showing 55.04% WR / −$2.25/tr / −$827 sum; the "DO NOT DEPLOY" verdict text is at lines 59 and 67-69 (not line 37 literally, but the −$2.25 figure and the negative verdict are accurate). (3) AUDIT_FINAL_CORRECTED_2026_05_29.md has no "§E" section label, but the content is real: line 104 lists `btc_5m_sniper_hod` at −$267 lifetime PnL, and Priority Action #1 (line 133) explicitly says "KILL active bleeders: ... sniper_hod (pending HoD refresh)." (4) gates.py line 44 confirms HOD_TOP8_BY_CELL for ("sniper","btc_5m") = (1,2,4,6,8,14,21,22). Severity is downgraded from critical to high because: (a) the sleeve runs in `mode="paper"` (main.py line 1797) — it is shadow/paper only, not live capital; (b) the audit itself categorises the kill reason as "HoD lists stale — re-judge after refresh" (§G, line 119), not an irredeemable strategy failure, so the KILL is contingent on a HoD refresh that was never built. The pre-deploy backtest did produce a negative $/tr, the sleeve was never killed as instructed, and it continues to accumulate negative shadow PnL — that is a real process failure. But "critical" overstates it because no real money is at risk and the kill recommendation itself was explicitly held pending a HoD list refresh.

The wiring is correct (main.py:117 and gates.py:43 both verified), but the fee-model claim in the audit finding is factually wrong and overstates the discrepancy. The "backtest" figure of WR 55.78% / +$1.64/tr (from HANDOFF_2026_05_22_HOD_REFRESH_SLEEVE_FIXES.md line 68) was produced by shadow_11_sleeves_v2.py, which reads actual live poly_updown_resolution events from trading_events_30d.parquet and uses the pnl_usd already computed by the live resolver — it does NOT run a synthetic 2%-fee model. Both the "backtest" and the live 7d measurements use the same fee (the live resolver's slot_resolution_pnl, which applies the 0.07·p·(1−p) curve per AUDIT_FINAL_CORRECTED_2026_05_29.md CORRECTION 1). There is no fee-model divergence to account for. The real issue is simpler: the 55.78% WR figure is in-sample — derived from the same 28-day window used to select the HOD top-8 hours. HANDOFF_2026_05_22 line 172 explicitly flags this: "Out-of-sample window: refreshed-HoD numbers are in-sample on the same 28d used to derive the hours. Need a 7-day forward-walk before live deploy." The live 7d WR of 0.448 is OOS for an in-sample-selected filter, which accounts for most of the gap. At n=87, z ≈ −2.05 (p ≈ 0.04), so the OOS underperformance is statistically real but not extreme, consistent with normal HOD in-sample overfitting rather than a code or fee bug. Severity is medium (real OOS edge degradation, not a critical implementation flaw).
verdict.evidence: main.py:117 confirms wiring matches claim. gates.py:43 confirms HOD list (0,2,10,12,15,17,18,21) is deployed correctly — matches the May 22 refreshed fire-time-anchor list. shadow_11_sleeves_v2.py lines 215-224 show the 55.78% figure comes from live event pnl_usd, not a synthetic fee model. AUDIT_FINAL_CORRECTED_2026_05_29.md CORRECTION 1 confirms 0.07 curve is the live fee (no 2% legacy in play). verdict.note: The HOD-staleness attribution is factually wrong, but the live underperformance is real. Code check: `main.py:110` wires the sleeve correctly as `("poly_updown_btc_15m_sniper_hod", "sniper", "BTC", "15m", ("hod",), "sniper", "HEDGE_HOLD")` — exact match to spec. `gates.py:47` has `("sniper", "btc_15m"): (0, 7, 9, 13, 14, 16, 18, 19)`, which is NOT the original spec table `[0, 3, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15]` but IS the intentionally refreshed table from `HOD_REFRESH_2026_05_22.md` (line 24) and `TV_AGENT_PHASE34_FIXES_2026_05_22.md §2.2`, operator-approved on 2026-05-22 as the first fire-time-anchor refresh. The cited 57.23% WR / +$5.43/tr backtest (`SHADOW_11_SLEEVES_V2_2026_05_22.md` row 14) was computed WITH that same refreshed table — so production is running exactly the hours the backtest was validated on. The AUDIT_FINAL_CORRECTED §G claim that "stale HoD lists" explain the underperformance is incorrect for this sleeve. The actual residual concerns are: (1) the 57.23% backtest is in-sample over the same 28d event window used to pick the top-8 hours — genuine OOS live period shows 40.5% WR on n=37, a ~2.1 SD gap that is statistically marginal but not conclusive; (2) fee model attribution is a non-issue here since the shadow_11_sleeves_v2.py backtest reads `pnl_usd` directly from live events rather than applying a fee model. The discrepancy is real (live is losing) but the mechanism is in-sample overfitting in the HOD derivation, not a code bug or stale constant. Severity is medium rather than high: the sleeve is paper-only, no live capital at risk, n=37 is too small to distinguish bad luck from broken edge at high confidence.

audit.engine_summary: The fast_taker family runs inside the sniper-v5 loop (engine/main.py:2637 `poly_sniper_v5_loop`). Signal anchor: `slot_start + offset_s` (intra-window, NOT the momo ws_s). Fee model: sniper_v5 sleeves route through `MakerFillSimulator`; b2_nomerge comment (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1424) says "legacy_2pct" (2%-on-winning-profit); LAGV2 comment (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1498-1499) says "0.07 winner-only fee". Fill model: live WS BookMirror snapshot via `paper.get_orderbook_snapshot` 3-tier path. Spread filter: same-token `ask0-bid0` (direction is `_SPREAD_BTC=0.02` for b2_nomerge BTC, `_SPREAD_ETH=0.02` for b2_nomerge ETH, `_SPREAD_LAGV2=0.05` for all lagv2 sleeves; sniper_v5_sleeves.py:197-203). Sizing: flat `notional_usd_override=Decimal('2.0')` for b2_nomerge, `Decimal('25.0')` for lagv2 (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1467,1484,1513,1538,1563,1588). Exit: b2_nomerge=HOLD (hold to resolution); lagv2=LAG_REVERSAL_STOP with reversal_stop_bps=10.0. Signal gate for BOTH families reads `oracle_lag.price_delta_bps` from `compute_oracle_lag()` (engine/oracle_lag.py:160) = `(binance_feed - chainlink_oracle) / oracle * 10_000` (feed-vs-oracle basis). g_oracle_lag_bps_ge (gates.py:740-774) used by b2_nomerge: pass iff abs(price_delta_bps) >= 3.0 AND direction matches sign. g_oracle_lag_with (gates.py:805-835) used by lagv2: pass iff 3.0 <= abs(price_delta_bps) <= 12.0 AND direction matches sign. Both gates also require `oracle_lag.stale=False` (5s threshold, oracle_lag.py:57,164). RTDS feed (polymarket_rtds) started in engine as `poly_sniper_v5.oracle_lag_rtds_feed` task (main.py:2632-2635). Outcome resolution: chainlink via poly_updown_resolver. One_shot_per_slug=True for b2_nomerge and all lagv2.

invariant_findings.invariant: 1. SIGNAL ANCHOR
invariant_findings.detail: fast_taker family correctly anchors at slot_start + offset_s (intra-window), NOT at ws_s. This is the spec-correct anchor for this strategy: the sniper-v5 loop dispatches at slot_start_us + offset_s, confirmed in main.py wiring (main.py:2637) and in the sleeve definitions (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1465,1510). The momo ws_s=(slot_start-window_s) lookahead risk does NOT apply here. The ACTUAL bug for lagv2 is the gate signal content (see invariant 2 / sleeve findings), not the timestamp anchor.

invariant_findings.invariant: 2. FEE MODEL
invariant_findings.detail: Three-way conflict. (A) All lag_taker backtests used FEE_RATE=0.07 winner-only curve: lag_taker_foundation_2026_05_29.py:67, lag_taker_stoploss_sizing_ph2b_2026_05_29.py:51, lag_taker_oos_reval_2026_06_01.py:76. (B) LAGV2 live spec (TV_AGENT_SPEC_FAST_TAKER_LAGV2_2026_05_29.md §5) says fee='0.07 winner-only curve (the verified production fee)' and sleeve comment at sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1498 says '0.07 winner-only fee'. (C) b2_nomerge live spec (TV_AGENT_SPEC_FAST_TAKER_SHADOW_AB_2026_05_29.md §4) says fee=legacy_2pct (2%-on-winning-profit), and sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1424 comment reads 'Fee model legacy_2pct'. CLAUDE.md (operator note 2026-06-01) says live uses '0.07 curve: pnl_won=(1-vwap)*shares*(1-0.07*vwap)'. The actual engine fee dispatch depends on tv_poly_maker_fee_model env var (poly_maker_fill_sim.py:843,918). Without seeing the live .env the exact fee charged is unknown, but the LAGV2 backtest and the b2_nomerge backtest BOTH used 0.07 yet the b2_nomerge spec says legacy_2pct — this is a live-vs-backtest discrepancy for b2_nomerge that will overstate live PnL vs the 0.07-curve backtest by ~$0.43/trade at typical vwap=0.69.

invariant_findings.invariant: 3. L25 FILL + SPREAD FILTER
invariant_findings.detail: Live uses WS BookMirror (Tier-1 WS mirror per CLAUDE.md) via paper.get_orderbook_snapshot; this matches the sniper-v5 fill model. Spread filter is same-token ask0-bid0 (correct for a directional taker — cross-token check explicitly excluded per spec TV_AGENT_SPEC_FAST_TAKER_SHADOW_AB_2026_05_29.md §8). Live spread values: b2_nomerge=0.02 (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:197-198), lagv2=0.05 (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:203). These match the respective specs exactly. The subsample_1hz issue does not apply (sniper-v5 uses WS BookMirror live events, not L25 parquet). The cross-token spread discrepancy (CLAUDE.md invariant) is irrelevant for this family.

invariant_findings.invariant: 4. OUTCOME RESOLUTION
invariant_findings.detail: Chainlink via poly_updown_resolver, consistent across all fast_taker sleeves (main.py:2573-2588, _sniper_v5_oracle_resolve function). NOT binance close. Matches spec and CLAUDE.md convention.

invariant_findings.invariant: 5. DATA STALENESS
invariant_findings.detail: oracle_lag feed depends on polymarket_rtds (binance WS price + chainlink RTDS). The RTDS feed is started as a dedicated task (main.py:2632-2635 `poly_sniper_v5.oracle_lag_rtds_feed`). Stale guard: oracle_lag.stale=True when chainlink_age_s > 5.0s (oracle_lag.py:57,164) → gate returns False (sniper_v5_gates.py:824). No dependence on HL liquidations or SOL 5m panel (relevant for other families, not this one). No DATA_GAP from stale feeds for this family.

invariant_findings.invariant: 6. SIZING / EXIT
invariant_findings.detail: Sizing: b2_nomerge uses $2 flat (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1467,1484) per spec. LAGV2 uses $25 flat (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1513,1538,1563,1588) per spec. Both correct. Exit: b2_nomerge uses default HOLD (hold to resolution, no reversal stop); lagv2 uses LAG_REVERSAL_STOP with reversal_stop_bps=10.0. The lagv2 exit spec (TV_AGENT_SPEC_FAST_TAKER_LAGV2_2026_05_29.md §3.3) specifies the reversal stop should be measured on the ORACLE_LAG (feed-vs-oracle) basis: 'snap = compute_oracle_lag(slot.asset, now_us)'. The fix spec (TV_AGENT_FIX_LAGV2_SIGNAL_2026_06_01.md §3) requires the reversal stop to be switched to the INTRA-WINDOW BINANCE RETURN basis for consistency with the corrected signal. Since the signal bug is not yet fixed (see sleeve findings), the reversal_stop is also measuring the wrong quantity — it compares feed-vs-oracle at exit to feed-vs-oracle at entry, not binance intra-window return. This is a secondary bug contingent on the primary signal bug being fixed.

This is the feed-vs-oracle basis, not the backtested intra-window binance return delta_bps=(px_fire/px_open-1)*1e4. On the live box chainlink oracle/strike reads BELOW the live binance feed (the oracle lags behind), so price_delta_bps sits persistently in the [+3,+12] UP band on every slot — direction sign always UP. The fix (Option 1/2 in fix spec) has NOT been applied in this snapshot — sniper_v5_gates.py still contains the original g_oracle_lag_with using oracle_lag.price_delta_bps with no binance intra-window return path. No g_binance_lag_with function exists in the gates file. Additional bug: reversal_stop (LAG_REVERSAL_STOP, reversal_stop_bps=10.0 at sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1515) also measures reversal on feed-vs-oracle basis not intra-window return (fix spec §3). Fee: 0.07 winner-only used in backtest (lag_taker_foundation_2026_05_29.py:67) which matches sleeve comment (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1498), but env-var governed (poly_maker_fill_sim.py:843).
