The bug is real and exactly as described. Code evidence: `g_oracle_lag_with` (sniper_v5_gates.py:831-835) reads `bps = float(oracle_lag.price_delta_bps)` and sets `leading = "UP" if bps > 0 else "DOWN"`. `compute_oracle_lag` (oracle_lag.py:160-164) defines `price_delta_bps = (feed_price − oracle_price) / oracle_price × 10000` — a feed-vs-chainlink basis, not the intra-window binance return that was backtested. On a live market this basis is persistently positive (chainlink oracle lags an upward-drifting feed), so every evaluation lands in the [+3,+12] UP band and never the [-12,-3] DOWN band → 100% UP fires. The ETH sleeve (sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1557-1580) is structurally identical to BTC 5m: same `g_oracle_lag_with(3.0,12.0)` gate, same `g_cross_asset_lag_confluence(3.0)` reading BTC's `oracle_lag_other.price_delta_bps` (also persistently positive, reinforcing the UP bias rather than filtering it). The `oracle_lag.py` docstring "ETH/SOL out of scope for Phase 28" is documentary only — `compute_oracle_lag("ETH",...)` has no ETH-specific code guard and will produce a valid snapshot if ETH prices are in `polymarket_rtds`; the real failure is the shared one-sided basis signal, not missing ETH price data. The `firing_sleeves_7d.csv` shows `poly_fast_taker_lagv2_eth_5m` at n=3, WR=1.000: consistent with small-sample luck on an always-UP bet during a period ETH closed UP, exactly as the claim asserts. `LAGV2_ROOTCAUSE_ALWAYS_UP_2026_06_01.md` corroborates with 95 resolved fires across all 4 LAGV2 sleeves showing 0 DOWN fires. The reversal-stop secondary bug is also confirmed: `maybe_reversal_stop` measures reversal via `compute_oracle_lag(...).price_delta_bps` (same feed-vs-oracle basis, symmetric flip ≈ impossible in a trending market), so the stop is effectively dead. Severity remains critical because the sleeve has no directional edge — it is a coin-flip always betting UP on $25 notional.

The bug is real and code-verified. The direction-selector gate `g_oracle_lag_with` at `sniper_v5_gates.py:831` reads `bps = float(oracle_lag.price_delta_bps)`, which `oracle_lag.py:160-162` computes as `(feed_price - oracle_price) / oracle_price * 10_000` — a feed-vs-chainlink-oracle basis. On the live box this quantity is persistently positive (chainlink oracle lags an upward-drifting binance feed), so `abs(bps)` always lands in the `[3,12]` UP band and never the DOWN band, causing the sleeve to fire 100% UP. The btc_15m sleeve definition at `sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1532-1555` is identical to btc_5m (same gate `g_oracle_lag_with(3.0,12.0)` as the first/direction-selector GateRef, same four-gate stack), so it inherits the exact same defect. `firing_sleeves_7d.csv` confirms n=1, blank WR (unresolved) as of the snapshot — consistent with the sleeve having just launched. `LAGV2_ROOTCAUSE_ALWAYS_UP_2026_06_01.md` reports n=15 at 13.3% WR from the wider DB audit (all UP, no DOWN). The backtested signal was a different quantity — the intra-window binance return `(binance_close(slot_start+offset)/binance_close(slot_start) - 1) * 1e4`, which swings symmetrically ±, producing ~50/50 UP/DOWN and 68% WR. The substitution of `price_delta_bps` (feed-vs-oracle) for the intra-window return was flagged in `TV_AGENT_SPEC_FAST_TAKER_LAGV2_2026_05_29.md §2.1` as "the better signal, shadow will confirm" — it was never confirmed before deployment. verdict.evidence: sniper_v5_gates.py:740-774 confirms g_oracle_lag_bps_ge is logically direction-aware (line 774: `return (direction == "UP") if bps > 0 else (direction == "DOWN")`), so the claim that the gate code itself is wrong is a mischaracterization — the gate function is correct. However, the bug is real and critical: it lives in the runtime input. oracle_lag.py:160-162 shows price_delta_bps = (feed_price - oracle_price) / oracle_price * 10_000, i.e., live binance spot minus the chainlink oracle price. On the live box the chainlink oracle/strike reference is pinned to the most recent resolution price (not the current spot), so binance feed sits persistently above it — price_delta_bps is structurally positive every slot, making g_oracle_lag_bps_ge fire UP on 100% of evaluations. The fix spec TV_AGENT_FIX_LAGV2_SIGNAL_2026_06_01.md §1 explicitly documents this: "oracle_lag_bps logged None on every one (a second, logging bug)" and "bps lands in the [+3,+12] UP band every slot and never the [-12,-3] DOWN band". firing_sleeves_7d.csv line 140 confirms n=4, WR=0.25 for b2_nomerge_btc_5m (first fire 2026-06-01 19:01 UTC+2), consistent with forced-UP direction on a ~50% resolution rate. The additional fee-model sub-claim (spec calls for legacy_2pct per TV_AGENT_SPEC_FAST_TAKER_SHADOW_AB_2026_05_29.md lines 176-178 and 192) is correctly specified in the shadow spec; any discrepancy with the backtest script itself could not be verified from the snapshot files present, but this is a secondary concern that does not change the severity of the primary signal bug.
verdict.note: The signal bug is confirmed critical. The gate function g_oracle_lag_bps_ge at sniper_v5_gates.py:774 is logically correct (direction-conditional), but its runtime input oracle_lag.price_delta_bps (defined in oracle_lag.py:160-162 as (binance_feed - chainlink_oracle) / chainlink_oracle * 10_000) is structurally and persistently positive on the live box because the chainlink oracle reference is pinned to the last resolved strike price, not the current spot — meaning the live binance feed will always be above it, so bps is always in the positive/UP band and the gate always fires UP regardless of direction. Live data (firing_sleeves_7d.csv: n=4, WR=0.25, all fires on 2026-06-01) is consistent with forced-UP on a near-50% outcome base rate. The fix spec correctly diagnoses the problem as a signal substitution error — the backtest used intra-window binance return (slot_start to fire, symmetric ±) while the live implementation feeds feed-vs-oracle basis (one-sided positive). The fix must replace the oracle_lag input with the intra-window binance return for all 4 A/B family sleeves (both g_oracle_lag_bps_ge users). The fee model claim in the audit is accurate per spec: TV_AGENT_SPEC_FAST_TAKER_SHADOW_AB_2026_05_29.md §4 specifies legacy_2pct, not 0.07.

The always-UP bug is real and code-verified, but the cited "594 fires" figure belongs to the sibling sleeve `a25_merge_eth_5m`, not to `b2_nomerge_eth_5m`. The fix spec table (`TV_AGENT_FIX_LAGV2_SIGNAL_2026_06_01.md` line 13) lists counts in order `a25_merge_btc_5m/a25_merge_eth_5m/b2_nomerge_btc_5m/b2_nomerge_eth_5m = 602/594/702/264`; `b2_nomerge_eth_5m` had 264 all-UP fires, not 594. The root cause is confirmed by reading the gate directly: `sniper_v5_gates.py:771` does `bps = float(oracle_lag.price_delta_bps)` and `sniper_v5_gates.py:773-774` returns UP iff `bps > 0`, while `engine/oracle_lag.py:160-162` computes `price_delta_bps = (feed_price - oracle_price) / oracle_price * 10_000` — a feed-vs-oracle basis that sits persistently positive (live binance feed above chainlink strike), so the gate passes UP on every slot and never reaches the DOWN branch. The sleeve definition at `sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1487-1493` uses exactly this gate with `threshold_bps=3.0`, direction=BOTH, confirming the mechanism is identical to the BTC sibling. WR of 0.500 at n=4 is consistent with chance, not with the backtested 68% signal. The bug is critical: the sleeve fires as a pure coin-flip (no signal at all) while consuming shadow capital and polluting WR statistics. The only minor inaccuracy in the original claim is the wrong fire count (594 vs the correct 264).

verdict.note: The audit contains multiple errors that together over-state the concern. (1) The cited live statistics are wrong: DEPLOY_PORTFOLIO_BY_MARKET_2026_06_01.md line 26 shows n=35, WR 94.3%, Sharpe 0.39 — the audit's n=42 / 95.2% figures appear in no file in the repo. (2) The gate code is genuinely correct: sniper_v5_sleeves.py:391-401 shows exactly g_dir_down + g_mp_skew_strong_with (|skew|>50 bps, bearish) + g_tr_stack_full_with(BTC) (stack_score==-2), offset=600, spread=0.02, matching the fidelity audit row 11 MATCH at FIDELITY_AUDIT_V5_V9_2026_05_29.md:30. (3) The "high-implied-prob pick-only" hypothesis is unsupported by the gate definitions: unlike several other sleeves, this sleeve has NO g_entry_vwap_in_band gate, so it does not select on market probability level; a full bear EMA stack + strong bearish microprice at t=600s is a structural condition independent of the DOWN token's CLOB price. At t=600s into a 15m slot with a full bear stack the DOWN implied probability is typically 0.65-0.80, not 0.92+, so WR 94% > implied_p represents real edge, not a zero-EV tautology. (4) The fee model discrepancy (live HOLD path uses 0.07*vwap not legacy 2%) is real and already documented as Bug 4/5 in the fidelity audit; it makes shadow PnL ~2.7% conservative relative to production, meaning actual live profits would be slightly higher, not lower — this is a logging artefact, not a bias inflating apparent WR. The remaining genuine concern is simply the small sample (n=35), which is a normal OOS-validation gap, not evidence of hidden bias.

audit.engine_summary:
Signal anchor: Kalshi EMA gates (g_tr_above_ema50/800) look up the TradersRealityPanel at fire_us (window_start_us + offset_s*1e6). For offset=600 this is 10 min into the 900s window — not pre-window, not post-window, no lookahead. Correct causal anchor.

Fee formula: KalshiEventLogger._pnl (kalshi_event_logger.py:183-191) computes won→(1.0-vwap)*shares-flat_fee, lost→-vwap*shares-flat_fee. This is the raw Kalshi payout (NO Polymarket fee curve). The flat fee is from tv_kalshi_fee_usd_per_fill (default 0.0) set at main.py:2799. Kalshi's actual fee schedule is not encoded — fee_usd_per_fill=0 unless configured, meaning paper PnL is overstated on won fires by the Kalshi platform fee.

Fill model: Kalshi uses a KalshiMarketDataFeed (native Kalshi WS book), not the Polymarket L25 book. The controller calls client methods on the Kalshi exchange. No L25 walk; Kalshi orders use the Kalshi CLOB. This is correct for live Kalshi but means backtests using Poly L25 fill model are not directly comparable.

Spread filter: each Kalshi sleeve has spread_filter=Decimal('0.02') (sniper_kalshi_sleeves.py:64,107). How the controller evaluates this against the Kalshi book is in KalshiUpdownController (NOT present in the snapshot), so cannot be verified. The Poly sniper v5 uses same-token ask0-bid0; the live cross-token spread concern (CLAUDE.md) does not directly apply to Kalshi (single token per direction).

Sizing: notional_usd=getattr(settings,'tv_kalshi_notional_usd',5) (main.py:2798), default $5. No notional_usd_override on any Kalshi sleeve. Per V10 spec the operator chose $1/fire — this is a runtime config that must be set via TV_KALSHI_NOTIONAL_USD=1; if not set, defaults to $5.

Exit: base sleeve HOLD (hold-to-resolve), _H sleeve HEDGE_LATE (kalshi_loop._hedge_late_then_resolve scheduled at window_end-60s, kalshi_loop.py:267-273). Resolution is via controller.resolve(sleeve,ticker) after window_end+60s buffer (kalshi_loop.py:328-348).

invariant_findings.invariant: 1. SIGNAL ANCHOR (ws_s vs slot_start vs fire_us)
invariant_findings.detail: Kalshi fires are offset-anchored (offset=600s for ema sleeves, offset=60s for S4). The EMA/TR gates in g_tr_above_ema50/800 call tr_panel.lookup(asset, fire_us) where fire_us = window_start_us + 600*1e6. This is 10 min into the 900s window — not pre-window, so no lookahead vs the EMA signal. The S4 prewindow sampling happens at slot_start-120s (kalshi_loop.py:178) and caches the signal for the later in-window fire — causal. The Kalshi loop does NOT use ws_s convention (that is Polymarket-specific); the EMA-down strategy does not require ws_s anchoring. No lookahead detected.

invariant_findings.invariant: 2. FEE MODEL
invariant_findings.detail: BACKTEST (24_ema_down_fullperiod.py:13) uses 0.07-curve: pnl_won = shares*(1-entry)*(1-0.07*entry), pnl_lost = -shares*entry. LIVE (kalshi_event_logger.py:189-191) uses raw payout: pnl_won = (1-vwap)*shares - flat_fee, pnl_lost = -vwap*shares - flat_fee, with flat_fee defaulting to 0.0 (main.py:2799 tv_kalshi_fee_usd_per_fill). The live formula is the raw Kalshi market payout with zero fee correction. Kalshi charges its own fee schedule (not the 0.07 Poly curve and not the legacy 2% Poly rule). The backtest overstates expected PnL by the omitted Kalshi fee. Additionally CLAUDE.md says the Poly live engine uses 2%-on-winning-leg (not 0.07 curve) for Polymarket markets, but for Kalshi neither is definitively correct — the actual Kalshi fee needs to be encoded in fee_usd_per_fill or the pnl formula. Current setup leaves fee_usd_per_fill=0 unless operator sets TV_KALSHI_FEE_USD_PER_FILL.

invariant_findings.invariant: 3. L25 FILL and SPREAD FILTER
invariant_findings.detail: Kalshi sleeves use the Kalshi native WS book (KalshiMarketDataFeed), not Polymarket L25. The L25 10Hz/subsample_1hz and the cross-token spread invariant are Polymarket-specific and do not apply to the Kalshi controller. Kalshi has a single YES/NO book per market. The spread_filter=Decimal('0.02') on each sleeve (sniper_kalshi_sleeves.py:64,107,89) is the same value as Poly sniper, but its evaluation against the Kalshi book is inside KalshiUpdownController (not in snapshot). Backtest used Poly L25 fill model with 0.07-curve on Poly books — not equivalent to live Kalshi fills. This is a known and documented cross-venue difference (V10 spec §OPERATOR DEPLOYMENT DECISION note), not a hidden bug.

invariant_findings.invariant: 4. OUTCOME RESOLUTION = Chainlink Data Streams
invariant_findings.detail: KalshiUpdownController is not in the snapshot; resolution method cannot be verified from available files. The kalshi_event_logger.py (line 171) defers to controller.resolve(sleeve,ticker) whose implementation is absent. Kalshi markets resolve via Kalshi's own oracle (NOT Chainlink). The Kalshi family does not use chainlink_rtds. This is expected for a different venue, but it means the Kalshi resolution is NOT Chainlink-backed — the invariant as stated (Chainlink for Polymarket) is inapplicable to Kalshi by design. No evidence of a bug here; it is a deliberate different venue.

invariant_findings.invariant: 5. DATA STALENESS (HL liqs, SOL 5m timestamp, missing universe panel)
invariant_findings.detail: The Kalshi family uses only EMA50/EMA800 gates from TradersRealityPanel and the S4 prewindow signal from binance feed. Neither depends on HL liquidations (stale since May 27), ETH chainlink basis, or SOL 5m universe panel. The EMA panel is fed by the live Binance 1m kline stream. Main.py:2311-2312 notes 'EMA-gated Kalshi/sniper sleeves go blind' if the 1s stream is off — but the 1m EMA feeds are from a separate kline provider. No data staleness risk identified for the two EMA sleeves. The S4 sleeve depends on binance VWAP dev_bps (binance_feed at main.py:2873) and potentially the Poly book (via poly_prewindow_ctx_fn); both feeds are live.

invariant_findings.invariant: 6. SIZING / EXIT
invariant_findings.detail: SIZING: V10 spec (TV_AGENT_SPEC_EMA_DOWN_V10_2026_06_01.md §OPERATOR DEPLOYMENT DECISION) specifies $1/fire for Kalshi V10 live deployment. Main.py:2798 sets notional_usd=getattr(settings,'tv_kalshi_notional_usd',5) — default $5. If TV_KALSHI_NOTIONAL_USD=1 is not set in the env, all three Kalshi sleeves fire at $5 instead of the spec's $1. Cannot confirm from the snapshot whether the env var is set. EXIT: base sleeve HOLD (correct per spec). _H sleeve HEDGE_LATE is wired via kalshi_loop._hedge_late_then_resolve (kalshi_loop.py:284-318), checks at window_end-lead_s=60s. hedge_late_check_lead_s defaults to 60 (SniperV5Sleeve dataclass default, no override on the _H Kalshi sleeve) — matches spec 'final-30s-if-bid<0.6x' intent at a 60s lead. S4 sleeve fires and resolves via normal _resolve_after_window path (no special exit); correct for a shadow sleeve.

verdict.note: All core claims verify against the actual code. (1) Entry-band gate: `sniper_kalshi_sleeves.py:56-77` defines the live sleeve with exactly three gates — `g_dir_down`, `g_tr_above_ema50(BTC)`, `g_tr_above_ema800(BTC)` — no entry-band gate anywhere in the tuple. The V10 Kalshi sleeve (`kalshi_sniper_btc_15m_ema50_ema800_off600_down_V10`) called for in the spec was never added to the snapshot; the file contains only the parent and the `_H` HEDGE_LATE variant, both band-free. (2) Existing gate constants: `sniper_v5_thresholds.py:105-116` shows `VWAP_BAND_LOW_THR=0.20`/`HIGH=0.80` and `VWAP_NARROW_LOW_THR=0.15`/`HIGH=0.55` — neither pair matches the spec's [0.15, 0.93] or [0.15, 0.95], and neither is imported into `sniper_kalshi_sleeves.py`. (3) Spec itself is internally inconsistent: `TV_AGENT_SPEC_EMA_DOWN_V10_2026_06_01.md` line 5 (Operator Decision) says band cap = 0.93; lines 15/37/52 (body, backtest table, acceptance criteria) say 0.95. So even the intended threshold is ambiguous. (4) Fee discrepancy is real but partially mitigated by context: backtest `24_ema_down_fullperiod.py:13` applies `0.07·p·(1−p)` curve; `kalshi_event_logger.py:183-191` uses raw `(1−vwap)·shares − fee` with `fee_usd_per_fill=0.0` default (no curve). However, CLAUDE.md notes that on Kalshi crypto up-down markets the effective fee rate may also be near zero, so the absolute PnL gap may be small in practice — severity of the fee sub-claim is lower than the missing gate. The dominant issue is the unimplemented V10 sleeve: the live Kalshi sleeve is running the unfiltered parent, exposing all deep-lottery (<0.15) and no-upside-favorite (>0.93) fires that V10 was designed to exclude.

The live _H sleeve at sniper_kalshi_sleeves.py:96-109 is correct-by-design: it carries exactly the same 3-gate stack as the base _down sleeve (g_dir_down + g_tr_above_ema50(BTC) + g_tr_above_ema800(BTC)) with exit_policy="HEDGE_LATE" (line 108), which is intentional — the _H sleeve is the A/B control twin for the exit-policy experiment, not the V10 band variant. HEDGE_LATE scheduling is confirmed correct in kalshi_loop.py:258-273 (hedge_late branch on fire_result.all_gates_passed, lead_s defaulting to 60 via sniper_v5_sleeves.py:173). The entry-band [0.15, 0.93] was NEVER supposed to live on the base _H sleeve: TV_AGENT_SPEC_EMA_DOWN_V10_2026_06_01.md §"Sleeves to create" calls for a *separate* sleeve kalshi_sniper_btc_15m_ema50_ema800_off600_down_H_V10 (a clone of _H with the band gate added). That V10 sleeve — along with all 3 other EMA-down V10 siblings — does not exist anywhere in the engine snapshot (confirmed by grep across all .py files and families.json). The real discrepancy is unimplemented V10 family (4 sleeves absent), not a misconfigured gate on the live _H sleeve, which is operating as designed. Severity is medium rather than high: no live sleeve is misbehaving; the gap is a missing shadow-deploy upgrade.

audit.engine_summary:
SIGNAL ANCHOR: The live engine fires at fire_us = slot.slot_start_us + offset_s * 1_000_000 (loop:145). All gates receive fire_us directly (e.g. regime_panel.lookup(asset, tf, fire_us), tr_panel.lookup(asset, fire_us)). The pre-window gate g_pw_trend_slope_with correctly subtracts window_s to get ws_s_us (gates.py:1287). No F7-style momo signal anchor is relevant here — these are sniper sleeves with book/technical gates, not momo RSI gates. There is no ws_s lookahead risk for this family.

FEE MODEL: The live controller (PolymarketSniperV5Controller, not in snapshot) is not directly readable. The backtest scripts (14_fullperiod_persistence.py:16, 16_eth_newgates_mdd.py:9) use the 0.07 curve: pnl_won = shares*(1-vwap)*(1 - 0.07*vwap). CLAUDE.md states production historically uses legacy 2%-on-profit-only and the handoff (2026-06-01) confirms live uses 0.07*p*(1-p) winner-only. Both backtest and live appear to use the same 0.07 formula — no mismatch detected between backtest files and stated live behavior.

L25 FILL: Live reads the BookMirror WS at fire_us (synchronous book_mirror.get(token)); controller is wired with book_mirror at main.py:2389. Spread filter is the same-token ask0-bid0 spread via sniper_v5_sleeves.py's spread_filter field (ETH=0.02, VL_ETH=0.025). This is the SAME-TOKEN spread, matching the engine_v2 backtest convention (not the cross-token live updown convention). No discrepancy for this family.

SIZING: Default notional = settings.tv_poly_sniper_v5_notional_usd (logged at main.py:2657). Sleeve-level override via notional_usd_override (sleeves.py:164). For ETH 5m family, no notional overrides are set — all sleeves use the global default.

EXIT: All ETH 5m sniper sleeves use exit_policy='HOLD' (default) — hold to slot_end then oracle resolve (loop.py:170-194). The loop correctly dispatches _resolve_at_slot_end for HOLD sleeves. HEDGE_LATE and LAG_REVERSAL_STOP paths exist but are not used by any ETH 5m sleeve.

OUTCOME RESOLUTION: Resolved via onchain oracle (OnchainOracle.get_resolution via _sniper_v5_resolve, main.py:2570-2588) which reads Chainlink CTF payoutNumerators. Correct.

PANEL WARMUP (CRITICAL): VolHurstPanel is constructed empty at boot (main.py:2232) and fed only by 1m bars. For 5m hurst_60, warmup requires 60×5m = 5 HOURS of continuous uptime. The panel seeding (seed_1m_handlers_from_rest, main.py:2299) seeds REGIME/SMS/VWAP/F7/RF1h from 4-day REST history, which should warm hurst panels too IF binance_feed.seed_1m_handlers_from_rest correctly replays through vol_hurst.on_1m_bar. However, HANDOFF_HURST_HLCASCADE_FIX_2026_06_01.md:29-32 confirms that as of 2026-06-01, SOL 5m hurst was still not warming after restarts — implying the seed may not always reach the vol_hurst handler for all assets.

invariant_findings.invariant: 1. SIGNAL ANCHOR — sniper sleeves use fire_us = slot_start_us + offset_s, no momo ws_s anchor needed
invariant_findings.detail: Sniper-v5 gates receive fire_us directly. No RSI/F7 anchor is involved in any ETH 5m sniper sleeve. The pre-window gate g_pw_trend_slope_with correctly anchors at ws_s_us = slot_start_us - window_s (gates.py:1287). No lookahead risk identified for this family.

invariant_findings.invariant: 2. FEE MODEL — backtest uses 0.07 curve; live engine should match
invariant_findings.detail: Both the validation backtests (14_fullperiod_persistence.py:16, 16_eth_newgates_mdd.py:9) and the HANDOFF_2026_06_01 operator note confirm the 0.07*p*(1-p) winner-only formula. The controller (not in snapshot) is stated in the handoff to use this same formula. No mismatch between backtest and live is evident. Caveat: the controller code itself is not in the snapshot so this cannot be verified at the code level.

invariant_findings.invariant: 3. L25 FILL + SPREAD FILTER — live uses BookMirror WS same-token spread; backtest should match
invariant_findings.detail: ETH 5m sleeves have spread_filter=0.02 (VL variants=0.025) as a same-token ask-bid check in sniper_v5_sleeves.py. This matches the engine_v2 backtest convention. The cross-token spread mismatch issue from CLAUDE.md applies to the poly_updown loop, not to sniper-v5 which uses the sniper-native fill path (book_mirror direct). No discrepancy for this family.

invariant_findings.invariant: 4. OUTCOME RESOLUTION — must use Chainlink Data Streams, not binance close
invariant_findings.detail: Resolution via OnchainOracle.get_resolution (main.py:2570-2588) reads CTF payoutNumerators — the Polymarket on-chain settlement which is Chainlink-sourced. Correct.

invariant_findings.invariant: 5. DATA STALENESS — VolHurst/hlcascade/ETH chainlink basis feeds
invariant_findings.detail: Two staleness issues confirmed: (A) hurst_60 in VolHurstPanel requires 5h warmup after restart (HANDOFF_HURST_HLCASCADE_FIX_2026_06_01.md:29-32). The seed_1m_handlers_from_rest should warm this but the handoff reports SOL hurst is still cold post-restart, suggesting the seed may be unreliable. Affects g_hurst_trending / g_hurst_reverting / g_hurst_regime_with gates used by 10+ ETH 5m sleeves. If hurst_60 is None, all hurst gates return False → sleeves with hurst-only gates may fire less or not at all post-restart. (B) For hlcascade ETH sleeves: bybit+bitget liquidation feeds are empty (HANDOFF:61-68), delivering ~50-70% fewer liquidations. Affects eth_5m_a2_hlcascade50k_v9 and up_a2_hlcascade25k_v9.

invariant_findings.invariant: 6. SIZING / EXIT — intended_size_usd, exit_type correctness
invariant_findings.detail: All ETH 5m sleeves use exit_policy='HOLD' (default in SniperV5Sleeve dataclass, sleeves.py:171). None of the ETH 5m family has HEDGE_LATE or LAG_REVERSAL_STOP. The loop correctly routes HOLD sleeves to _resolve_at_slot_end (loop.py:187-194). Sizing uses global settings.tv_poly_sniper_v5_notional_usd with no per-sleeve overrides for the ETH 5m family (notional_usd_override=None for all). All exits are hold-to-resolve.

verdict.note: The discrepancy is real — live WR ~51% vs backtest 82-89% is massive — but the claimed mechanisms are wrong or overstated. Code check: `sniper_v5_sleeves.py:1035-1046` confirms VL_01 is an exact copy of the parent (V8_05 at line 886-895) with only `spread_filter` changed from `_SPREAD_ETH=0.02` to `_SPREAD_VL_ETH=0.025`; all four gates (`g_hurst_regime_with`, `g_trend_slope_with`, `g_cci_with`, `g_tod_europe_us_window`) are identical and their kwargs are correct. The prior fidelity audit (`FIDELITY_AUDIT_VL_2026_05_29.md` row #1) independently confirmed PASS. CCI seeding: `main.py:2321` calls `seed_1s_handlers_from_rest(minutes=120)` at boot — 7200 seconds of seed data for a 60s CCI window; `TAIndicatorsPanel.on_1s_bar` is registered at main.py:2255. The claim that 1s seeding is "insufficient or stale" is refuted by the code. VL vs parent comparison: WR 51.3% (VL) is actually marginally *above* parent WR 48.6%, not below it — the claim that VL underperforms vs parent is inverted. ETH 5m hurst cold-start: the 5h warmup (60 bars × 5min, documented in `HANDOFF_HURST_HLCASCADE_FIX_2026_06_01.md`) does apply, but 39 fires exist, confirming the panel does warm up; the cold period just suppresses fires correctly. The real issue is plain OOS degradation of the parent sleeve V8_05: it was backtested on Apr 24 – May 26 at 82-89% WR, and has underperformed at ~50% WR since live deployment. The VL variant is faithfully copying that parent and shares the same OOS underperformance. Severity is downgraded from high to medium because there is no engineering bug, no gate misconfiguration, and VL is not specifically worse than its parent; the problem is a backtest-vs-live gap that affects both equally and requires re-evaluation of whether the V8_05 signal retains edge in the current OOS window.

The gate structure at sniper_v5_sleeves.py:885-896 and sniper_v5_gates.py:1071-1087 is correctly cited. However, three sub-claims are wrong or overstated. First, the cold-start / warmup attribution is incorrect for ETH 5m: main.py:2283-2305 shows the engine calls seed_1m_handlers_from_rest(days=4) on boot, which replays 4 days (5760 1m-bars) through all 1m-panel handlers including VolHurstPanel; the 60-bar 5m warmup requires only 300 1m-bars, so ETH 5m hurst_60 is always warm after restart. The SOL warmup bug in HANDOFF_HURST_HLCASCADE_FIX_2026_06_01.md is explicitly scoped to SOL (where a prior FIX 4 hit the wrong layer), not ETH. Second, the claim says "if hurst_60 is cold → always False → sleeve still fires (other gates pass)" — this is internally contradictory: g_hurst_regime_with returning False blocks all-gates-pass, so the sleeve would NOT fire. The fact that 35 fires occurred confirms hurst_60 was warm and ≥ 0.55 on those occasions. Third, the claim that "edge appears absent" is statistically premature: binomtest(17, 35, 0.5, two-sided) gives p=1.0, and the 95% CI for WR is [33%, 66%], which is fully consistent with both a coin flip and a genuine 65-70% WR edge dampened by small-sample variance. The feed-gap root cause is real and confirmed, but the claim's characterization of "11 fires on noisy/incomplete signal" is inverted — the gate did not fire at all for ETH. audit.engine_summary: SIGNAL ANCHOR: All 5 VWAP sleeves fire via `build_bar_context_t_plus_n` (poly_updown_loop.py:1122). The fire moment is `ws_s + offset_s` (line 1152: `fire_us = (ws_s + offset_s) * 1_000_000`), where `ws_s` is the slot_start boundary (bar-close). This is NOT a lookahead — ws_s is the already-closed bar. VWAP deviation is computed from 1s binance closes in Vwap15mStore at the fire moment. RSI-14 is fetched at offsets [-840..0] from ws_s (poly_updown_loop.py:1207-1212), matching the F7 spec. M1V regime is computed at ws_s (line 1224). FEE MODEL (LIVE): the resolver uses `slot_resolution_pnl` from `backend.app.venues.polymarket.fees` (poly_updown_resolver.py:67), which the resolver's comment explicitly calls 'the 2% Polymarket fee' (line 34). However, HANDOFF_2026_06_01 (operator-confirmed) states the live engine NOW uses the `0.07*p*(1-p)` winner-only curve — this means resolution PnL = `(1-vwap)*shares*(1 - 0.07*vwap)` on wins and `-vwap*shares` on losses. The snapshot cannot confirm which formula `slot_resolution_pnl` implements (fees.py not in snapshot), but the audit reports confirm 0.07 curve is live. FILL MODEL: 1s binance WS BookMirror via `executor.get_orderbook_snapshot` (line 1272); fired with `enable_1s_stream=True` when `TV_POLY_VWAP_CONT_ENABLED=true` (main.py:1422-1428). SPREAD FILTER: pre-computed per direction by `_spread_pct` imported from `backend.app.controllers.polymarket_updown` (not in snapshot); the pre-computed `spread_pct_yes/no` fields are set in BarContext (loop:1281-1282). The live controller spread check is same-token bid-ask (per `_spread_pct` semantics), not cross-token. SIZING: flat `mode='paper'`, `hedge_policy='HOLD_ONLY'` for all 5 sleeves (main.py:1851). Each sleeve has `slot_allowlist=frozenset([(asset, tf)])` (main.py:1854-1855) and `audit_sleeve_id` (line 1857). EXIT: HOLD_ONLY — hold to resolution, no hedge/sell. DISPATCH: master scheduler (when `TV_POLY_USE_MASTER_SCHEDULER=true`) routes vwap_continuation controllers through `_fire_t_plus_n_boundary` (loop:1909) keyed by (tf, offset_s); dedup on ws_s. AUX WIRING BUG (critical, documented): `polymarket_updown.py:_build_signal_aux()` had no `vwap_continuation` branch, so strategy.signal() received a v3/sniper aux dict missing `bar_ctx_phase` and all vwap fields. Phase gate `if aux.get('bar_ctx_phase') != expected_phase` fired NONE on 100% of evals. Fires started 2026-06-01 (first fires in firing_sleeves_7d.csv all timestamped June 1), confirming the fix was applied today but is uncommitted on VPS3.

verdict.note: All cited evidence holds up under direct code inspection. `inverse.py:136-140` confirms the live controller gates only on `is_night_hour_utc()` with no per-(signal, day-of-week) cell discrimination: for `inverse_volume_night` it simply returns `flip_signal(base_signal)` whenever the bar window falls in NIGHT_HOURS_UTC={1,2,3,4,5,9,10}, unconditionally for UP and DOWN signals on any day. The GA `volume_INV_NIGHT_all.csv` (both runs momo_ga_1779280108 and momo_ga_1779280445) confirms that of the 8 btc_5m cells (signal×hour_bucket×dow_group), 4 cells are SKIP, 1 is single-fold KEEP (UP 00-05 weekend, active_folds=2), 1 is KEEP (DOWN 06-11 weekday), and 2 are INVERT (UP 00-05 weekday and UP 06-11 weekday) — only the two INVERT cells are coherent with the live sleeve's flip, while the SKIP and KEEP cells dilute the edge. The leak-free Tier A analysis (`FINAL_DEPLOY_LEAK_FREE_2026_05_20.md` §37-53) certified exactly zero btc_5m cells; only `btc_15m UP 06-11 weekday → INVERT` passed FDR (perm p=0.0005, BH rank 1 of 1). One claim detail is imprecise: the night-hour gate itself IS correctly implemented in code — the structural flaw is the absence of signal-direction and day-of-week filtering within the night window, not misfiring outside night hours. The fire count (525 over 7 days vs 588 theoretical max for night-only) is consistent with the hour gate working. The 0.478 WR and −$958 PnL in `families.json` are genuine: SKIP cells generate fires that the GA said should be silent, cancelling out the INVERT-direction edge of the profitable UP-weekday cells.

The discrepancy is real and the code evidence is clear. `strategies/polymarket/inverse.py:136-140` shows `apply_inverse_filter` for `inverse_volume_night` fires on ALL base signals (UP and DOWN) during night hours: it checks only `is_night_hour_utc(window_start_unix)` then unconditionally calls `flip_signal(base_signal)` — there is zero direction-level filtering. The GA optimizer output at `strategy_lab/ga_optimizer/runs/momo_ga_1779280108/volume_INV_NIGHT_all.csv` lines 22-25 shows all 4 ETH-5m DOWN-signal cells (00-05 weekday/weekend, 06-11 weekday/weekend) labelled `SKIP`, and line 29 (UP 06-11 weekend) also `SKIP`; only 3 of 8 cells are active (INVERT or KEEP). The live controller registration at `engine/main.py:1739-1746` constructs the inverse controller with `mode="paper"`, `strategy_mode=inv_mode` and nothing else — no `gate_cell_strategy` parameter is passed, unlike the Phase-34 shadow controllers at `main.py:1794-1806` which do receive `gate_cell_strategy`. The original spec (`strategy_lab/reports/TV_AGENT_INVERSE_SLEEVES_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1) specified flipping ALL UP/DOWN night-hour signals with no direction filter, so the live code correctly implements that original spec; the gap is that the GA optimizer's post-hoc direction-level SKIP findings were never fed back as a filter. Severity is high (not critical) because these are confirmed paper-only sleeves (`mode="paper"`, `executor=paper_executor`) with no real capital, but the consequence is analytically damaging: ~50% of the 524 recorded live fires come from DOWN-signal cells the backtest said to skip, diluting the aggregate WR to ~0.49 and making the live dataset unsuitable for validating whether the INVERT cells (UP 00-05 weekday, UP 06-11 weekday) actually hold their predicted ~60% edge.

verdict.note: The code at `vps3_engine_snapshot_2026_06_01/strategies/polymarket/inverse.py:136-140` is exactly as cited. The `apply_inverse_filter` function for `inverse_volume_night` checks only `is_night_hour_utc(window_start_unix)` — i.e., whether the bar window's UTC hour is in `NIGHT_HOURS_UTC = {1,2,3,4,5,9,10}` (line 46). There is zero weekday/weekend discrimination and zero direction (UP vs DOWN) discrimination. The GA optimizer CSV (`ga_optimizer/runs/momo_ga_1779280108/volume_INV_NIGHT_all.csv`, lines 35-42) shows that for SOL 5m the worst cell — DOWN|00-05|weekday — has inv_sel=-821 and action=SKIP, yet it receives hours 1-5 from the live gate and fires indiscriminately. `firing_sleeves_7d.csv` line 11 confirms 494 live fires at WR=0.464, pnl=-1571.71. The claim's description of the mechanism is accurate: the live night-hour gate was designed before the GA discovered that DOW and direction subcells have very different outcomes; those sub-cell decisions were never back-propagated into `apply_inverse_filter`. Severity remains high: 494 live fires, -$1,572 paper loss, driven by a structural mismatch between the deployed filter (hour-only) and the backtest-validated cell structure (hour × direction × DOW).
